entry.title: Long-lived light-driven bimagnon pairs at finite momentum in NiO
entry.summary: Long-lived light-driven bimagnons at finite momentum in NiO arXiv · Nov 13, 2026Researchers pumped NiO with mid-infrared pulses far below its bandgap to excite phonon-assisted two-magnon absorption, then probed the resulting dynamics with time-resolved resonant inelastic X-ray scattering. The one-magnon linewidth and energy stayed essentially unchanged, indicating preserved long-range magnetic order. A pump-induced two-magnon signal peaks about 4 ps after excitation and decays with a time constant of 28±11 ps, far longer than previously reported two-magnon dephasing times.

entry.title: Discrete time crystals stabilized by anti-unitary periodic driving and dynamical freezing
entry.summary: Discrete Time Crystals from Anti-Unitary Floquet Driving and Dynamical Freezing arXiv · Nov 13, 2026The paper proposes stabilizing a discrete time crystal using anti-unitary periodic driving, through a mechanism called dynamical freezing. Magnetization emerges as a conserved operator, and an exact pairing of two-cycle quasi-energies locks in the subharmonic response. Infinite-chain simulations show no detectable decay for generic states with finite magnetization. An outline of an experimental realization of the anti-unitary drive is also given.

entry.title: Ensemble phase transitions in measurement-unitary hybrid quantum circuits
entry.summary: Ensemble phase transitions in measurement-unitary hybrid quantum circuits arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies hybrid quantum circuits that alternate unitary evolution with projective measurements, examining an ancillary qubit entangled with the system. It analyses two state ensembles: the trajectory ensemble conditioned on measurement outcomes and the projected ensemble generated by final-boundary measurements. Both ensembles undergo non-analytic ensemble phase transitions at the measurement-induced purification critical point, even though their first moments remain maximally mixed.

entry.title: Quantum Metrology and Quantum Battery in a Hyperfine-Coupled Spin System
entry.summary: Quantum Metrology and Quantum Battery in a Hyperfine-Coupled Spin System arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies an effective electron-proton spin system inspired by the hydrogen atom's hyperfine structure, examining both multiparameter quantum metrology and energy storage. The authors treat the external magnetic field and hyperfine coupling strength as unknown parameters, deriving the quantum Fisher information matrix and quantum Cramér-Rao bounds for their joint estimation. They also characterize the system's ergotropy, anti-ergotropy, storage capacity, and energy-basis coherence under a unitary charging protocol.

entry.title: Statistics of correlation lengths in the many-body localised phase's Fock space
entry.summary: Statistics of Fock-space correlation lengths in the many-body localised phase arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies long-range many-body resonances in the many-body localised phase of disordered quantum systems, which appear as strong inhomogeneities in eigenstate amplitudes on Fock space. The authors develop a microscopic theory based on two-point Fock-space correlation functions and apply exact diagonalisation to the disordered tilted-field Ising chain. They find that typical correlations decay exponentially, while average correlations decay subexponentially with system-size dependence driven by rare resonant nodes.

entry.title: Traces of vacuum squeezing: a superconducting circuit that mimics particle creation in the early universe
entry.summary: Traces of Vacuum Squeezing: A Superconducting Transmission-Line Analogue of Cosmological Particle Creation arXiv · Nov 13, 2026The paper proposes a superconducting transmission line loaded with dc-SQUIDs as an analogue of a scalar field in a radiation-dominated expanding universe. Its mode equation reduces to the Weber equation, which has an exact solution in parabolic cylinder functions and an exponentially suppressed particle spectrum. The authors show that the anomalous moment of each mode witnesses Bogoliubov mixing and survives dissipation.

entry.title: Sharp uniform Fisher information bounds from projective designs
entry.summary: Sharp Uniform Fisher Information Bounds from Projective Designs arXiv · Nov 13, 2026The paper studies fixed measurements for multiparameter pure-state metrology that stay informative without knowing the input state. It defines the Fisher floor as the smallest fraction of quantum Fisher information retained across all pure states and tangent directions. Bounds on this floor are derived from projective design order alone, and they approach one half, the single-copy quantum limit, as the order increases. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive dimension-independent Fisher floor guarantees from projective design order, reporting tightness at order two and odd orders, with applications to pure-state estimation.

entry.title: Near-optimal multiparameter quantum metrology using a fixed small number of measurement bases
entry.summary: Near-Optimal Multiparameter Pure-State Metrology with a Constant Number of Bases arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies multiparameter pure-state quantum metrology, where measurements optimized for different parameters are incompatible. It introduces the Fisher floor, the smallest fraction of quantum Fisher information retained across all pure states and parameter directions, as a measure of uniform sensitivity. The authors prove that a constant number of fixed orthonormal bases, independent of the Hilbert-space dimension, achieves a nearly optimal Fisher floor. They also show that d+1 mutually unbiased bases, when they exist, have a Fisher floor of at most 1/(d+1), so optimal average balance does not ensure uniform sensitivity. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show a constant number of fixed orthonormal bases yields a dimension-independent near-optimal Fisher floor, with tight bounds and a contrast to MUBs.

entry.title: Stiffness in Confined Quantum Walks: how boundaries shape spreading
entry.summary: Stiffness in Confined Quantum Walks arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies discrete-time quantum walks confined to a finite lattice by unitary reflecting boundaries built from coin-flip operations. The authors define a dimensionless spreading stiffness and compare localized, Gaussian, and truncated-uniform initial states. They find that long-time behavior depends strongly on the initial profile, and that dynamical stiffness and spatial homogenization are distinct properties.

entry.title: Observing genuine multi-time quantum memory: a quantum memory effect that only appears when three or more times are examined together
entry.summary: Observation of Genuine Multi-Time Quantum Memory arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies memory effects in open quantum systems, noting that non-Markovian dynamics alone does not prove quantum memory, since classical-memory models can reproduce it. The authors show that some quantum memory escapes all tests comparing two times and becomes detectable only when three or more times are considered jointly. They derive an analytical three-time witness and experimentally demonstrate this hierarchy on a superconducting-qubit platform with time-independent couplings. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce quantum memory detectable only via three-time witnesses, derive an analytical witness, and report experimental demonstration on superconducting qubits.

entry.title: A four-city quantum key network in Slovakia that delivers keys in real time and is checked against finite-key security limits
entry.summary: A deployed four-city entanglement-based QKD network with real-time key delivery, benchmarked against finite-key security bounds arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper reports the entanglement-based part of Slovakia's national quantum communication infrastructure, linking four cities in western Slovakia over deployed telecom fiber. Entangled photons from a central node are routed by wavelength to form a fully meshed network of three cities without trusted relays, with the fourth city connected through the central node. Keys are delivered in real time via ETSI GS QKD 014, and reported rates are measured after full post-processing. The implemented scheme is also benchmarked against finite-key security bounds.

entry.title: Scalable Pauli propagation via F₂-linear partitioning
entry.summary: Scalable Pauli propagation through 𝔽₂-linear partitioning arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper presents a parallelization method for Pauli propagation, which simulates quantum circuits by evolving observables as sparse sums of Pauli strings. The authors partition the strings with an F₂-linear hash function, so each gate application splits into independent tasks with bounded communication. Benchmarks of their open-source implementation show efficient parallel scaling within and across compute nodes, handling over 10^11 Pauli strings.

entry.title: Non-interferometric tests of gravity-related decoherence using mechanical oscillators
entry.summary: Non-interferometric tests of gravitational decoherence models with mechanical oscillators arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies three phenomenological models of quantum-gravity-induced decoherence, based on deformed relativistic symmetries, stochastic metric fluctuations, and a stochastic generalized uncertainty principle. For a harmonic oscillator, the models cause anomalous heating with qualitatively different energy dynamics. The authors compare the models with existing mechanical platforms and conclude that heating and continuous measurements are complementary non-interferometric probes of gravity-related decoherence.

entry.title: Experimental 1D Gaussian-modulated CV-QKD with finite-size parameter estimation
entry.summary: Implementation of a 1D Gaussian-modulated CV-QKD under finite-size parameter estimation arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper experimentally demonstrates a one-dimensional Gaussian-modulated continuous-variable quantum key distribution system over 12 km of standard single-mode fiber. It uses a local local oscillator architecture with independent lasers and a full processing chain including coherent detection, reconciliation, parameter estimation, and privacy amplification. The system achieves privacy-amplified rates of 1.421 Mbit/s under asymptotic security and 0.364 Mbit/s under the finite-size scenario.

entry.title: Quantum Boltzmann equation for static electron correlation with cumulant closure
entry.summary: Quantum Boltzmann Equation for Static Correlation with Cumulant Kernel Closure arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper proposes a Quantum Boltzmann Equation for static electron correlation, mapping the BBGKY hierarchy onto discrete atomic-orbital matrix mechanics. The two-body cumulant is projected onto its lowest unitary invariant and relaxed toward a hyperbolic-tangent attractor via Markovian collisional relaxation, giving a parameter-free cumulant kernel. The method is tested on the H3 exchange reaction, H4 dissociation, BeH2, H2O and N2 bond cleavage, an 11-molecule dissociation set, and benzyne diradical isomers. The authors report that the kinetic relaxation resolves strong static correlation at zero electronic temperature.

entry.title: Explicit maximally entangled states in dimensions twice a prime power
entry.summary: Explicit Absolutely Maximally Entangled states in dimensions twice a prime power arXiv · Nov 13, 2026The paper constructs explicit families of absolutely maximally entangled (AME) states for multipartite systems with local dimension 2q, where q is an odd prime power, using a coupling of qubits and q-level systems. It gives AME(N,2q) results for several party numbers and, together with known inputs, completes the classification for nine parties: an AME(9,d) state exists if and only if d is at least 3. ★★★★ Notable: The authors construct AME states in dimension 2q via a qubit-qudit coupling and report completing the nine-party classification with several explicit parameter families.

entry.title: Lattice response theory for subsystem symmetry-protected topological phases
entry.summary: Lattice response theory for subsystem symmetry-protected topological phases arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper develops a lattice response theory framework for studying subsystem symmetry-protected topological (SSPT) phases. It builds spacetime lattice gauge fields from X-type symmetry actions on qudit systems and shows that a gauge-invariant response action yields an entangler that stacks the corresponding SSPT phase. The authors also construct a new 3+1d SSPT phase protected by two 2-foliated planar subsystem symmetries and a global 0-form symmetry. ★★★★ Notable: The authors develop a lattice response framework for subsystem SPT phases and construct a new 3+1d phase with a mixed 't Hooft anomaly.

entry.title: Efficient PEPS gradient computation for optimized quantum state preparation on 2D hardware topologies
entry.summary: Efficient computation of PEPS gradients for optimized quantum state preparation on 2D topologies arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper addresses preparing shallow quantum circuits for complex entangled states. The authors propose a topology-aware method that combines local disentanglement with global fine-tuning via gradient optimization of 2D projected entangled pair states (PEPS). They also describe an efficient procedure for computing PEPS gradients. Numerical simulations are used to test the method's convergence and performance.

entry.title: Generalized ladder operators and superintegrable systems built with Painlevé VI
entry.summary: Generalized ladder operators and construction of families of superintegrable systems with Painlevé VI arXiv · Nov 13, 2026The paper studies quantum Hamiltonians whose separated angular part is given by a generic Painlevé VI transcendent. It constructs generalized ladder operators for one-dimensional Schrödinger operators with a quadratic spectral variable. Combining these with radial shift operators yields higher-order integrals and deformed Racah-type polynomial algebras, giving new two-dimensional superintegrable families with Painlevé VI in the potential.

entry.title: Multi-particle quantum walk search on a two-dimensional lattice
entry.summary: Multi-particle quantum walk search on a two-dimensional lattice arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies how to formulate a search problem using multiple particles performing quantum walks and how efficient such search algorithms are. Each particle evolves in discrete time under Grover's quantum walk operator, with a focus on local interaction models where states change only when particles meet on the same grid site. The analysis centers on a two-dimensional grid and examines how the search's asymptotic success time and probability depend on interaction strength and maximal entanglement between particles. The authors report that two- and three-particle searches, with or without interactions, achieve a constant-factor improvement over the single-particle case, and they also propose a new generalized interaction model.

entry.title: Gaussian ergotropy as a probe of spatial correlations between accelerated vacuum and thermal fields
entry.summary: Gaussian ergotropy and spatial correlations: accelerated vacuum versus a thermal field arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies whether work extraction from two harmonic-oscillator detectors can reveal the spatial correlations of their environment, comparing an accelerated vacuum with an inertial thermal field of matching local spectrum. It links equilibrium Gaussian ergotropy to a response-weighted spatial correlation and proposes a two-setting scheme that reconstructs these correlations from work measurements.

entry.title: Noise-robust super-Heisenberg scaling in quantum sensing via subspace-twirled dynamical decoupling
entry.summary: Noise robust super-Heisenberg scaling in time-dependent quantum sensing by subspace-twirled dynamical decoupling arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies quantum parameter estimation using time-dependent Hamiltonians to achieve precision beyond the Heisenberg limit, known as the super-Heisenberg limit. The authors propose a dynamical decoupling scheme based on subspace twirling, which averages random unitaries over a subspace instead of the full Hilbert space, to preserve the encoding signal while removing environmental noise. They give conditions and performance guarantees for reaching super-Heisenberg scaling without adaptive control, and illustrate the results with a qubit sensor example.

entry.title: Physical observables and superselection rules
entry.summary: Physical Observables and Superselection arXiv · Nov 13, 2026Physical states are usually represented by unit vectors in a Hilbert space, and observables by self-adjoint operators. This paper reviews how superselection rules restrict which self-adjoint operators can represent observables, with consequences for states and the processes that transform them. It considers arguments for superselection rules arising from charge or possibly energy conservation, and discusses effective superselection rules arising from decoherence or the lack of a shared reference frame.

entry.title: Ergodicity breaking in a dissipative Ising model for data classification, with competing two- and four-body interactions
entry.summary: Ergodicity breaking for data classification in a dissipative Ising model with competing two- and four-body interactions arXiv · Nov 13, 2026The paper examines how data processing relates to the dynamics of interacting many-body systems. It studies an Ising model with competing two- and four-body interactions, whose dissipative evolution is described by a Lindblad master equation. Using mean-field calculations and exact small-scale numerics, the authors show that the stationary state manifold can be designed to enable multi-class classification. They also analyze the resulting basins of attraction, showing that the system can classify quantum states with nonlinear decision boundaries.

entry.title: Detecting entanglement via moments of the realigned state for continuous-variable systems
entry.summary: Entanglement detection from moments of the realigned state: application to continuous-variable quantum systems arXiv · Nov 13, 2026The paper introduces separability criteria based on singular and weak moments of the realigned density operator. The second-order moment criterion alone is found to detect entanglement in a wide range of quantum optical states. The moments can be measured with a linear interferometer that combines several identical copies of the state. The method's detection ability is illustrated for Gaussian and non-Gaussian states, including lossy NOON states.

entry.title: Improved low-cost quantum error mitigation using benchmarked-noise zero-noise extrapolation
entry.summary: Improved Low-Cost Quantum Error Mitigation with Benchmarked-Noise Zero-Noise Extrapolation (bnZNE) arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper theoretically extends and experimentally tests benchmarked-noise zero-noise extrapolation (bnZNE), a simple, low-cost method for reducing errors in quantum computations. It improves the classical extrapolation step to aim for better results than standard ZNE at the same total shot cost. Tests on IBM and IQM hardware across many large-scale applications found bnZNE consistently more accurate than standard ZNE.

entry.title: Lorentz Boosts and Field Equations of the Quantum Geometric Tensor in 4D Energy-Momentum Space
entry.summary: Lorentz Boosts and Governing Equations of the Quantum Geometric Tensor in 4D Energy-Momentum Space arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper extends the quantum geometric tensor, which combines the quantum metric and Berry curvature in solids, to four-dimensional energy-momentum space with frequency and momentum as independent coordinates. Its Lorentz transformation is fixed by the invariance of the real-spacetime plane-wave phase. Lorentz boosts of static Dirac and Weyl systems generate frequency metrics, shear metrics, and electric-like Berry-Maxwell fields. The authors derive governing field equations and flow conservation laws, and discuss experimental realizations in spacetime crystals or time-varying media.

entry.title: Statistics of coupled defects on lattices, where higher groups describe how defects of different dimensions interact
entry.summary: Higher-Group Statistics on Lattices arXiv · Nov 13, 2026The paper defines higher-group statistics on lattices as Berry phases of closed sequences of hopping operators. Its central example is a closed Majorana chain embedded in three dimensions, which gives a loop-flip process with phase +i. In two dimensions, charge-wall statistics distinguish two Z4 toric codes that have identical anyon statistics but different gauged theories. The authors also present two methods for generating statistical processes, which detect boundary anomalies of higher-group symmetry-protected topological phases.

entry.title: A unified master equation for driven multilevel quantum systems, with spectral signatures
entry.summary: Unified master equation for driven multilevel quantum systems: Derivation, dynamics, and spectral signatures arXiv · Nov 13, 2026The paper derives a unified master equation for arbitrarily driven multilevel quantum systems, using Lewis-Riesenfeld dynamical invariants within Born-Markov theory. It applies the equation to constant, periodically modulated, ramped and chirped Rabi-coupling protocols. Fluorescence spectra of a periodically driven three-level Λ system show features that conventional master equations miss. The authors attribute these shortcomings to inaccurate bath-frequency sampling and neglected nonsecular dissipative couplings, and identify parameter regimes that need a unified treatment.

entry.title: Qubit Communication Advantage in the Holevo-Frenkel-Weiner Scenario
entry.summary: Communication Supremacy of a Qubit in Holevo Frenkel Weiner Scenario arXiv · Nov 13, 2026The paper studies communication tasks in the Holevo-Frenkel-Weiner framework, asking whether a qubit can outperform a classical bit. It shows a qubit advantage without extra quantum resources such as entanglement, with shared classical randomness treated as free. The authors introduce a witness that separates quantum strategies from classical ones and examine the advantage under noise. They also link the advantage to the detection of coherence.

entry.title: Squeezed terahertz light from electron band nonparabolicity in ultrastrongly coupled 2D electrons
entry.summary: Squeezed terahertz light from nonlinear diamagnetism in ultrastrongly coupled two-dimensional electrons arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies two-dimensional electron gases in terahertz cavities, showing that electron band nonparabolicity turns the system into a quantum Kerr oscillator that can squeeze terahertz light. The authors use a non-rotating-wave theory with a self-consistent electron heating model, predicting 1.8 to 2.4 dB output squeezing for present GaAs samples. Improved mobility or cavity frequency could raise this to about 9 dB.

entry.title: When can local unitaries complete a state into an orthogonal basis?
entry.summary: When can local unitaries generate a complete orthogonal basis? arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies whether a multipartite pure quantum state can be completed to an orthonormal basis using only local unitary rotations, a property called universal local encodability (ULE). The authors prove that two-qutrit systems are universally locally encodable, resolving a previously open conjecture. They also construct universal local encodings for several other dimension combinations and give a necessary condition for universality in finite-dimensional multipartite systems.

entry.title: Symmetry-controlled critical states and localization in monitored superconductors
entry.summary: Symmetry-Controlled Criticality and Zeno Localization in a Monitored Quasiperiodic Superconductor arXiv · Nov 13, 2026The paper studies a continuously monitored model of free fermions with pairing, examining how quasiperiodicity affects localization and symmetry class. Using topological entanglement entropy as a probe of nonlocal correlations in quantum state diffusion simulations, the authors identify a transition between a critical phase and an area-law phase, with no transition in the clean limit. Deep in the Zeno regime, they derive an effective non-Hermitian Bogoliubov-de Gennes description and a closed-form localization length that agrees with numerics.

entry.title: A 2026 update mapping the global quantum technology company landscape
entry.summary: The landscape of quantum technology companies in 2026 arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper updates a 2022 study of 441 quantum technology companies, now covering 1,092 firms founded with a quantum focus, of which 935 remain active. Using public sources and archived websites, it examines company formation, technology fields, geography, acquisitions, closures, valuations, and links to AI, defence, and space. Computing software and applications remain the largest field, with suppliers and supporting businesses accounting for almost a third of active companies.

entry.title: Quantum Keynesian Beauty Contest with Continuous Variables
entry.summary: Quantum Keynesian Beauty Contest with Continuous Variables arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper uses quantum game theory to study speculative pricing in the Keynesian Beauty Contest, or p-Beauty Contest (p-BC). The authors implement the game with continuous-variable quantum systems, where increasing multimode squeezing transforms players' bids and reduces the boom-and-bust behavior that rational play produces for p above or below 1. They also show that a similar game can be built with classical channels and a global mediator, and analyze the cases of two, three, and many players.

entry.title: Hong-Ou-Mandel-like interference between two independent narrowband thermal states
entry.summary: Hong-Ou-Mandel-like interference between two independent narrowband thermal states arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper proposes a method to measure the frequency difference between two narrowband light sources at the single-photon power level, using Hong-Ou-Mandel-like interference between thermal states. The absolute value of the frequency difference can be extracted from temporal coincidence counts, and the results agree well with the authors' theoretical model. The beat signal of this interference resembles that of Hong-Ou-Mandel interference between two heralded single-photon sources, suggesting the method can locate zero detuning between such sources.

entry.title: Non-convex optimization using quantum tunneling search on a photonic chip
entry.summary: Non-Convex Optimization via Quantum Tunneling Search on a Photonic Chip arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper proposes quantum tunneling search (QTS), an algorithm combining quantum tunneling walks with local annealing to explore non-convex optimization landscapes. The authors map objective functions onto the potential term of a waveguide Hamiltonian by controlling refractive indices with femtosecond laser writing. Adding a varying Hamiltonian approach improves search efficiency and enables identification of the global minimum.

entry.title: Learning to control and predict light-driven electron-phonon dynamics
entry.summary: Learning to control and predict light-driven electron-phonon dynamics arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper presents a differentiable framework that combines optimization of driving fields with neural-network prediction in a two-site electron-phonon model. It compares piecewise-constant, B-spline, feed-forward, and recurrent control parameterizations, optimized to increase accumulated electronic double occupation. For the dissipation-free model at zero Hubbard interaction, all methods increase double occupation, with B-spline raising the mean total double occupation by about 30%.

entry.title: Free-space quantum key sharing over 18.9 km between cities through a dense urban area
entry.summary: Inter-city 18.9 km free-space QKD over a dense urban corridor arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper reports an experimental free-space quantum key distribution (QKD) link spanning 18.9 km across a densely populated area of the Barcelona metropolitan region. It uses a decoy-state BB84 system at 785 nm with room-temperature single-photon detectors and no adaptive optics at the receiver. In a 40-minute field test, the average channel attenuation was about 19 dB and the mean QBER was 1.31%, yielding an estimated average finite-size secret key rate above 11 kbit/s.

entry.title: Low-dimensional filtering for continuous quantum error correction via a classical control hierarchy
entry.summary: Reduced filtering using classical control hierarchy with linear optimality for continuous quantum error correction arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper addresses the complex model estimation that limits the practicality of continuous quantum error correction by recasting it as a classical control-theoretic state hierarchy. For any stabilizer code whose generators are all continuously monitored and driven by a single Pauli recovery channel, the authors prove that the exact filter closes at dimension 3·2^(n-k-1), a dimension set by the syndrome space. They also present a committed-recovery controller that needs only 2^(n-k) class probabilities and reports higher entanglement fidelity than the compared methods in the three-qubit bit-flip code and the five-qubit perfect code. ★★★★ Notable: The authors recast continuous quantum error correction filtering as a classical control hierarchy and report an exact filter dimension of 3·2^(n-k-1), a tight bound set by the syndrome space.

entry.title: Detecting non-Hermitian topology via long-time dynamics of open systems
entry.summary: Detecting non-Hermitian topology from long-time dynamics arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper proposes a method to measure a non-Hermitian topological invariant linked to the Lindbladian spectrum of open Gaussian systems with chiral symmetry, using the relaxation of the covariance matrix. The approach works in the long-time regime without isolating edge modes, so it still applies when the Liouvillian skin effect may hide them. The authors demonstrate the technique on a Kitaev chain with reservoir-induced nonreciprocity, deriving an analytical phase diagram, and show that the protocol reliably distinguishes all the phases.

entry.title: Ground-State Spin Squeezing and Collective Excitations in Z2-Symmetric Systems
entry.summary: Ground-State Spin Squeezing and Collective Excitations in ℤ₂-Symmetric Systems arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies spin squeezing in the ground state of many-body quantum systems, a resource for quantum-enhanced measurements. Using the anisotropic Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick model, the authors show that squeezing is set by the ratio of two transverse fluctuation costs, while the collective gap is set by their geometric mean. Analyses of XXZ chains and power-law interacting systems identify a branch where squeezing and gaps increase together and squeezing persists at higher temperatures. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive an exact link between squeezing and collective excitations, identifying a gap-opening branch, checked via exact diagonalization and spin-wave analysis on XXZ chains.

entry.title: Converting superpositions of nonorthogonal states with optimal probability
entry.summary: Probabilistic distillation of superposition arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies how superpositions of nonorthogonal states, such as optical cat states, can be converted into one another using operations that create no superpositions. The authors determine the optimal probability of such a conversion, which depends on how the components of the superposition interfere. The problem is fully solved for two reference states, and the paper also gives results for three or more reference states.

entry.title: Reply to a comment by Hradil and Řeháček on phase-sensing advantage
entry.summary: Reply to the Comment by Hradil and Řeháček arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This is a reply to a comment by Hradil and Řeháček. The commenters argued that the quantum metrological advantage in the authors' squeezed-vacuum phase-sensing experiment disappears once measurement repetitions and total photon resources are properly counted. The reply contends that this conclusion is mathematically unfounded and that neither resource accounting nor finite-sample statistics invalidate the demonstrated quantum-enhanced local phase sensitivity.

entry.title: Residual Entanglement vs. Residual Coherence: Neutrino Oscillations in Matter via Wave Packets
entry.summary: Residual Entanglement vs. Residual Coherence: A Wave Packet Approach in Neutrino Oscillation with Matter arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies quantum correlations in three-flavor neutrino oscillations in constant matter density using a wave-packet approach rather than the standard plane-wave description. It expresses residual l1-norm coherence, Concurrence Fill, and Three-π entanglement in terms of transition probabilities for an initial muon-flavor state, with calculations for the DUNE setup. Residual l1-norm coherence is found to dominate the entanglement measures. At very long distances, wave-packet decoherence washes out the oscillations and drives all measures toward averaged values.

entry.title: Thermodynamically consistent hybrid quantum-classical dynamics via metriplectic methods for generalized Lindblad and Bloch-Torrey equations
entry.summary: Thermodynamically Consistent Quantum-Classical Hybrid Dynamics: A Metriplectic Approach to Generalized Lindblad and Bloch-Torrey Equations arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper presents a metriplectic framework for hybrid quantum-classical dynamics that ensures thermodynamic consistency by conserving energy and producing non-negative entropy. It combines a hybrid Poisson bracket with a metriplectic 4-bracket, with quantum and classical subsystems coupled only through dissipative processes. Within this framework, the authors derive thermodynamically consistent generalizations of the Lindblad master equations and Bloch-Torrey equations for open quantum systems. The approach provides a unified description of quantum relaxation and classical diffusion, along with a clear interpretation of entropy production.

entry.title: Persistent-mediator architecture for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation with color codes
entry.summary: Persistent-mediator architecture for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation with color codes arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper proposes a cross-dimensional persistent-mediator architecture for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation using color codes. A 2D data register and a 3D mediator remain distinct encoded modules at each cycle boundary, coupled only through a transient protected subsystem. The authors combine a membrane-like joint-logical measurement with a cross-dimensional CZ gate, string-like surgery and feed-forward to close a deterministic logical T-gate cycle that avoids post-selection and destructive mediator readout, returning the 3D block to its initial logical state.

entry.title: Hilbert's 17th problem for symmetric functions: undecidability and a counterexample
entry.summary: Hilbert's 17th problem for symmetric functions: undecidability and a counterexample arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper studies inequalities between symmetric functions that hold for every number of variables. It proves that deciding whether a rational-coefficient symmetric function is nonnegative in all dimensions is undecidable, answering a question by Acevedo, Blekherman, Debus and Riener. It also presents a degree-8 homogeneous symmetric function that is positive definite in every dimension but has no sum-of-squares multiplier uniform in the number of variables. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors prove dimension-free nonnegativity of symmetric functions is undecidable and give a degree-8 counterexample to uniform sum-of-squares multipliers.

entry.title: Geometric theory of quasiperiodically driven quantum systems
entry.summary: Geometric Theory of Quasiperiodically Driven Systems arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper builds a general framework for quantum systems driven quasiperiodically, which lack a theory comparable to Floquet theory for periodic drives. Using counterdiabatic driving, the authors identify dynamically invariant spaces and decompose the evolution with an effective average-energy operator and gauge potential. They classify quasiperiodic drives into four classes by the geometry and topology of these spaces, extend Floquet's theorem to incommensurate drives, and propose ergodicity marked by coalescing invariant eigenspaces.

entry.title: Automatic O(a) improvement for Wilson twisted mass fermions in Hamiltonian formalism
entry.summary: Automatic O(a) Improvement for Wilson Twisted Mass Fermions in the Hamiltonian Formulation arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper applies a recently developed Symanzik effective Hamiltonian framework to Wilson twisted mass fermions. The effective Hamiltonian is built only from the symmetries of the lattice Hamiltonian, without using the Euclidean spacetime Symanzik effective action. The authors use it to prove automatic O(a) improvement at maximal twist and O(a) improvement via the mass and Wilson average. They also derive the structure of the O(a) counterterms needed for clover on-shell improvement of Wilson fermions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors apply a Hamiltonian Symanzik framework to Wilson twisted mass fermions, proving automatic O(a) improvement at maximal twist and finding the clover term splits into two independent coeffici

entry.title: Quantum tunneling of a measurement-driven active particle
entry.summary: Quantum tunneling of a measurement-driven active particle arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies a quantum active particle whose motion is locked to its spin orientation through spin-orbit coupling and damping, with the orientation kept persistent by continuous measurement via the quantum Zeno effect. Individual quantum trajectories therefore show active run-and-tumble motion. When the particle meets a potential barrier, its persistent velocity causes it to accumulate near the barrier, unlike a free quantum particle, which is reflected. The authors show that quantum tunneling raises this active particle's transmission rate above that of an analogous classical particle.

entry.title: A quantum algorithm for finding all eigenvalues and eigenstates of sparse matrices
entry.summary: A Quantum Algorithm for Computing All Eigenvalues and Eigenstates of Sparse Hermitian Matrices arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper presents a quantum algorithm that finds all distinct eigenvalues of a sparse Hermitian matrix and prepares a corresponding eigenstate in each eigenspace. Eigenvalues are output as binary strings at a prescribed precision, and eigenvectors are kept as quantum states rather than converted to classical vectors. The stated runtime is Õ(n s² log² n / Δ_min), where Δ_min is the minimum spectral gap, and the authors claim it beats the classical O(n³) approach under certain conditions.

entry.title: Identifying beauty and charm jets with a quantum circuit trained end to end on superconducting hardware
entry.summary: Beauty and charm jet identification with end-to-end training on a superconducting quantum processor arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper implements a variational quantum circuit to classify b- and c-jets from simulated LHCb data on a 5-qubit superconducting quantum computer at the Politecnico di Torino. All stages of the machine-learning workflow, including training and testing, run on the real quantum hardware. The authors report that hardware-induced quantum noise does not significantly degrade performance, and they propose a framework for evaluating training time and optimizing the circuit.

entry.title: Gatemon qubits built on in-situ ternary InAsSb/Al nanowire Josephson junctions
entry.summary: Gatemon qubits based on in-situ ternary InAsSb/Al nanowire Josephson junctions arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper realizes gatemon qubits using in-situ InAsSb/Al Josephson junctions formed in a single growth process. Gate-dependent microwave spectroscopy shows the qubit transition can be electrostatically tuned over several gigahertz. Rabi oscillations and Ramsey interference demonstrate coherent control, with representative T1 = 0.79 µs and T2* = 0.91 µs.

entry.title: Whether the channel RLD Fisher information bound can be reached asymptotically
entry.summary: Asymptotic Attainability of the Channel RLD Fisher-Information Bound arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies the channel right-logarithmic-derivative (RLD) Fisher information, a computable upper bound on the optimal asymptotic SLD Fisher information per channel use. It gives an exact equality criterion, a semidefinite feasibility condition involving only the Choi matrix and its first derivative. For generalized dephasing channels, the condition reduces to linear equations for nonnegative certificate weights. At a completely dephasing point, the authors compute optimal SLD information for every finite number of uses and show a repeated ancilla-free probe attains it, while the ratio of the two quantities can be unbounded. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give an exact semidefinite criterion for when the channel RLD Fisher bound is attained and compute optimal finite-use SLD information at a dephasing point.

entry.title: Superconducting qudits protected from noise using higher-harmonic Josephson junctions
entry.summary: Noise-Protected Superconducting Qudits from Higher-Harmonic Josephson Junctions arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies three-level superconducting qutrits built from a loop of three Josephson junctions, using the second harmonic of the current-phase relation to protect against relaxation. It presents two designs, one based on a small junction asymmetry and one using a small symmetry-breaking term, each with different trade-offs such as charge noise sensitivity. The authors identify altermagnetic Josephson junctions as a candidate platform and propose the sign of the second harmonic as a design principle for protected superconducting qudits.

entry.title: How atomic interactions affect quantum communication protocols
entry.summary: Effect of atomic interactions on quantum communication protocols arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper builds a first-principles framework for analyzing photonic quantum communication in an atomic medium, deriving an effective model for polarization-encoded single photons from a real-space quantization of the field coupled to two-level atoms. It applies the model to superdense coding, showing that the protocol capacity of a fixed Bell-state alphabet under erasure, dephasing, and depolarizing channels decreases monotonically with increasing atom-field coupling. For the BB84 quantum key distribution protocol, it proposes a modified version that discards erasure outcomes and derives the asymptotic key rate. The key rate decreases monotonically with coupling strength and vanishes beyond a finite critical coupling.

entry.title: Quantum Mpemba effect from logical information exposure in monitored circuits
entry.summary: Quantum Mpemba effect from logical-information exposure in monitored circuits arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper studies the Mpemba effect in a monitored Clifford chain, where a state starting farther from stationarity overtakes one starting closer. An unencoded Bell-pair state ends a cycle with lower mean entanglement entropy than a scrambled reference, with the gap growing linearly in chain length. The authors attribute the reversal to logical information exposure and certify the effect at 128 and 256 qubits using stationary-entropy bounds.

entry.title: Symmetry and quasi-gauge invariance of Krylov complexity
entry.summary: Symmetry and quasi-gauge invariance of Krylov complexity arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies Krylov spread complexity, which measures how widely a quantum system explores its Hilbert space during time evolution. The authors identify two classes of unitary transformations that leave this complexity unchanged and link this to the invariance of the initial state's energy distribution. For a localized initial state with a nondegenerate spectrum, the long-time average complexity equals (D-1)/2, where D is the Hilbert-space dimension.

entry.title: Learning graph states from local Pauli measurements, with tight limits for non-adaptive strategies
entry.summary: Learning Sparse Graph States with Local Pauli Measurements: Tight Nonadaptive Bounds and an Adaptive Separation arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper studies how many copies of an unknown n-qubit graph state are needed to identify its graph when each qubit is measured in the X, Y or Z basis. For nonadaptive strategies with d^3 ln n ≤ n, it shows that Ω(d^2 log n) copies are required, even with an unrestricted classical decoder and a small fraction of misreported edges. It also shows that adaptivity between copies can beat this barrier: on certain connected bipartite regular graphs with hidden bipartition, a breadth-first adaptive learner needs only O(d log^2 n / log log n) copies. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove a tight nonadaptive lower bound of Ω(d²log n) and an adaptive separation, answering an open question on graph-state learning.

entry.title: Circuit-level analysis of quantum error correction in second-generation quantum repeaters
entry.summary: Circuit-Level Analysis of Quantum Error Correction in Second-Generation Quantum Repeaters arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper presents a circuit-level simulation of second-generation quantum repeaters using stabilizer-based quantum error correction. It models a two-segment repeater link including encoding, syndrome extraction, decoding, and entanglement swapping. The authors compare the Steane and five-qubit codes under incoherent noise (depolarizing and dephasing) and coherent over-rotation errors. The Steane code performs better with coherent errors, while the five-qubit code achieves higher fidelity under low-level incoherent noise, and no code is best at higher noise levels.

entry.title: Designing bosonic steady states via Fock-space current engineering
entry.summary: Engineering Bosonic Steady States through Fock-Space Currents arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper presents a unified framework for autonomously stabilizing selectable Fock states, which are valuable resources in quantum technologies. The authors derive a stationary current-balance law that predicts a population background scaling inversely with Fock number and shows how a local current selectively enhances the target Fock-state population. Full quantum simulations support these predictions and demonstrate target-state populations building up autonomously from the vacuum.

entry.title: Testing whether quantum physics can break the Leggett-Garg limit
entry.summary: Probing the extreme quantum violation of the Leggett-Garg inequality arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The Leggett-Garg inequalities test the clash between macrorealism and quantum theory, and their maximal quantum violation is called the temporal Tsirelson bound. Some studies have claimed that this bound can be exceeded within quantum theory. This paper critically examines the reasoning behind these claims and finds conceptual shortcomings. Once these issues are addressed, the macrorealist bound reaches its algebraic maximum, so no violation of the bound occurs.

entry.title: Noise erodes the quadratic speedup of Grover search, shown analytically for local and coherent errors
entry.summary: Loss of the quadratic speedup in Grover search under local and coherent noise arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper analyzes how noise degrades Grover's quantum search algorithm, which gives a square-root query scaling over unstructured databases. It shows that global depolarizing noise reduces the coherent weight of the state without slowing the Grover rotation. For local noise, the tolerable error per qubit falls faster than the inverse square root of database size. For coherent rotation-angle errors, the success probability is bounded by a band that widens linearly with circuit depth.

entry.title: Learned eavesdropping detection in BB84 quantum key distribution does not converge
entry.summary: No Convergence in Learned Eavesdropping-Detection Dynamics for BB84 Quantum Key Distribution arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies a game between a reinforcement-learning eavesdropper and a threshold-adapting detector in BB84 quantum key distribution. Using alternating best-response training across three learning rules and three channel-noise levels, the authors find that detection performance keeps fluctuating and does not settle to a fixed point. They conclude that a learned detector cannot be certified from any single round, and that closing the stealth window may require changing the information structure rather than out-adapting the attacker.

entry.title: Creating and converting vortex light in coherently prepared hydrogen atoms and hydrogen-like ions
entry.summary: Generation and conversion of vortex light in coherently prepared hydrogen atoms and hydrogen-like ions arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper proposes a theoretical method for generating and converting optical vortices in a coherently prepared three-level Λ-type atomic medium. An azimuthally varying phase difference between two lower states adds phase winding to the generated light, so the output topological charge equals the input charge plus the coherence winding number. Analytical results and numerical examples using hydrogen transition parameters are presented, and under resonant conditions electromagnetically induced transparency is predicted.

entry.title: Training quantum neural networks one job at a time: making each cloud job count
entry.summary: Training quantum neural networks one job at a time arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper studies how a classical optimizer can make the most of each cloud job when training a quantum neural network classifier, since every round trip to a quantum processor is costly. The authors compare optimizers given equal job counts and shots per job, differing only in how each job's parameter batch is filled. A batched parameter-shift method needed fewer jobs than SPSA in simulation and reached SPSA's final training loss on IBM's ibm_fez processor, with clearly higher test accuracy at eight qubits.

entry.title: Unified quantum-network infrastructure using optical frequency combs
entry.summary: An optical-frequency-comb-enabled unified infrastructure for quantum networks arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper presents an infrastructure based on optical frequency combs that carries precision timing, classical communication and quantum communication over one shared fibre link. Classical data is encoded on the comb's intensity while its pulse timing is preserved, achieving 100 Mbit/s transmission and 0.85 fs timing stability at 1 s over 100 km. The authors also analyse the excess noise introduced into a co-propagating continuous-variable quantum key distribution channel, reporting 0.0037 shot noise units of added noise and a 6.7% secret-key-rate penalty after optimization. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors unify timing, classical data and CV-QKD on one comb-based fibre link, modeling added noise; the abstract reports 100 Mbit/s and 0.85 fs stability over 100 km.

entry.title: Collective information backflow inferred from local population records
entry.summary: Collective information backflow from a local population record: Identifiability and learning arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This study examines how information backflow in two identical qubits collectively coupled to a vacuum reservoir with an exponential correlation function can be inferred from population data. An ideal bright-state population trajectory determines the bath-parameter combinations relevant to a finite-time trace-distance backflow diagnostic, which sparse records can predict via learning or physical fitting. However, a two-hypothesis bound shows that finite measurement statistics prevent distinguishing reservoirs with similar short population records but substantially different backflow.

entry.title: Information thermodynamics for closed quantum many-body systems
entry.summary: Information Thermodynamics in Closed Quantum Many-Body Dynamics arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper builds an information-thermodynamic framework for closed quantum many-body systems that start in microscopic thermal equilibrium, using local measurements and finite-time controls. It proves that in the thermodynamic limit the extractable work matches that of the corresponding canonical ensemble, and expresses it via quantum-classical mutual information and Holevo information. The authors also show that feedback based on distant measurement outcomes can exploit hidden long-range correlations, extensively increasing extracted work relative to the canonical ensemble. ★★★★ Notable: The authors develop a framework for many-body quantum information thermodynamics, showing local feedback matches canonical extractable work and distant feedback exploits hidden long-range correlations

entry.title: Room-temperature optically detected spin coherence in the negatively charged gallium-vacancy (GaV⁻) in diamond
entry.summary: Optically-detected room-temperature spin-coherence from the GaV⁻ in diamond arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper reports the physical properties of GaV⁻, a newly discovered negatively charged gallium-vacancy defect in diamond, created by focused ion beam implantation and high-pressure high-temperature annealing. It shows optically detectable spin coherence at room temperature, with a T₂ of 1.06 microseconds, combining features of both nitrogen-vacancy and group IV vacancy defects. The authors position GaV⁻ as a promising resource for quantum sensing, networking, and computation.

entry.title: Noise-driven anti-Kibble-Zurek behavior with generalized stochastic resonance in a quantum Ising chain
entry.summary: Anti-Kibble-Zurek behavior driven by dichotomous Markov noise in a quantum Ising chain: Generalized stochastic resonance in the defect density arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies anti-Kibble-Zurek behavior in a quantum Ising chain under nonequilibrium critical quenches driven by dichotomous Markov noise, a prototypical non-Gaussian colored noise. The noise-induced defect density, used as the response function, is nonmonotonic in the correlation time and shows generalized stochastic resonance. The authors attribute this to sparse realizations of the noise in the slow-noise regime, a feature the power spectrum does not capture. The results reveal a fundamental difference between Gaussian and non-Gaussian noise in this setting.

entry.title: Infinite or indefinite: query cost of simulating the quantum switch
entry.summary: Infinite or indefinite: the query cost of simulating the quantum switch arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies how many calls to black-box operations a standard quantum circuit needs to reproduce the quantum switch, a device that applies two operations in a superposition of causal orders. For general channels on a d-dimensional system, the authors prove that no finite number of calls suffices for exact simulation in the worst case. They also show that approximation below error 1/2 requires a number of calls that grows with d. The paper further compares the switch with ordinary circuits in distinguishing two noise models with equal entanglement and gate fidelity. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors prove that circuits cannot exactly simulate the quantum switch with finitely many calls, give a d^{1/4} lower bound, and show a query advantage in noise discrimination.

entry.title: Quantum Control: methods for precisely steering quantum systems to target states
entry.summary: Quantum Control arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This chapter introduces quantum control, the precise steering of fragile quantum dynamics toward a desired final state or transformation. It covers the control problem, basic error sources, and methods for suppressing those errors. It then discusses state-of-the-art approaches such as adiabatic methods, quantum optimal control, and machine learning.

entry.title: How phase interference and transverse catalysts shape noise fragility in long-range variational quantum circuits
entry.summary: Phase Interference and Transverse Catalysts Govern the Noise Fragility of Long-Range Variational Quantum Circuits arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies how sensitive variational quantum circuits with long-range entangling gates are to a single fault. It argues that fragility depends on how fault phases interfere on the target Hamiltonian, not on how far faults spread. For Heisenberg chains, the authors prove that two faults with the same extensive support can cause either bounded or extensive energy damage, in the exact ratio N/2.

entry.title: Testing Quantum Advantage in High-Frequency Trading Using Market-Derived Nonlocal Games
entry.summary: Testing Quantum Advantage in High-Frequency Trading with Market-Derived Nonlocal Games arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper proposes market-derived nonlocal games, where the game's inputs and payoffs come from historical order-book data and backtests of joint actions rather than an idealized model. The method is demonstrated on a two-agent, three-stock cross-venue arbitrage setting. For the measured interaction scales, the game derived from observed market data shows no resolved quantum-classical gap. Controlled variations in liquidity competition and cross-stock repricing are used to identify regimes that support quantum advantage and to test whether it survives end-to-end backtesting on modified historical data.

entry.title: Testing superconducting single-photon detectors in very strong magnetic fields
entry.summary: Mapping the High-Field Response of Superconducting Nanowire Single-Photon Detectors arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This study tests a NbTiN superconducting nanowire single-photon detector in magnetic fields up to 14 tesla, adjusting the detector's orientation in situ and comparing results with normal operation at lower fields. Performance depends strongly on angle: perpendicular fields quickly shrink the usable bias-current range, while near-parallel alignment allows operation at higher total fields, keeping a finite margin up to 12 tesla and measurable dark counts at 14 tesla. The angular dependence is mainly governed by the perpendicular field component.

entry.title: Quantum search for new materials with target properties
entry.summary: Quantum Material Generation via Coherent Hamiltonian Search arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper introduces QMage, a quantum algorithm that searches over crystal compositions, unit cell structures, and atomic positions for configurations whose calculated properties meet target values within a set error tolerance. It uses a single coherent quantum circuit that block-encodes each configuration's Hamiltonian, isolates the target eigenstate, and amplifies satisfying configurations with fixed-point search. The authors design it for fault-tolerant quantum computers and estimate its cost in logical qubits and Toffoli depth. The approach generates candidates from first principles rather than generalizing from known materials.

entry.title: Shear strain's role in narrow Si/SiGe quantum wells for spin qubits
entry.summary: The importance of shear strain in narrow Si/SiGe quantum wells arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper studies the long-wavelength k1 term that couples conduction-band valleys in Si/SiGe quantum wells when paired with shear strain, and which governs Dresselhaus spin-orbit coupling. It shows that shear strain from metal top gates may be enough to activate this valley-coupling mechanism, reducing the need for ultrasharp interfaces. The authors propose a narrow quantum well scheme that avoids ultrasharp interfaces while still giving large valley splittings, spin-orbit couplings, and g-factor corrections.

entry.title: Communication inequalities for telling quantum from classical statistics with minimal setups
entry.summary: Communication inequalities: robust quantum advantage, measurement testing and dimension witnessing with minimal setups arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper derives dimensional inequalities that separate classical and quantum statistics in communication scenarios, a setting where no general separation method was previously known. The inequalities depend only on four parameters of the input-output statistics, corresponding to correlated and anticorrelated events. Under dimensional assumptions, saturating one inequality certifies SIC-POVMs with analytically derived noise robustness. The inequalities also serve as dimension witnesses for both correlated and anticorrelated statistics without requiring measurement incompatibility.

entry.title: Quantum geometric bounds and uncertainty relations for velocity variance and spread of Wannier functions
entry.summary: Quantum geometric bounds and uncertainty relations for velocity variance and spread of Wannier function arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper uses a derivation of the quantum Cramér-Rao bound and an argument by Efimov and Dodonov to derive uncertainty relations for mixed states. These constrain the diagonal product, trace, and individual diagonal elements of the covariance matrix of several observables. Choosing the symmetric logarithmic derivative as the observables yields geometric bounds on the quantum Fisher information matrix set by mean Uhlmann curvature, which become bounds on the quantum metric set by Berry curvature for pure states. The work also reveals optical sum rules for the velocity variance and spread of valence band Wannier functions, and verifies these bounds using spin canonical ensembles, topological materials, common semiconductors, and transition metal dichalcogenides.

entry.title: A comprehensive quantum electrodynamics study of fast electrons interacting with lossy nanostructures and quantum light
entry.summary: Comprehensive quantum electrodynamics of fast electrons interacting with dissipative nanostructures and quantum light arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper develops a quantum electrodynamical theory of how fast electrons interact with dissipative nanostructures. The authors use a modified Langevin noise formalism that quantizes scattering modes and material-generated fields independently, and derive a transverse-momentum-resolved energy exchange formula. They examine finite-temperature effects and report an intrinsic Stokes–anti-Stokes asymmetry in the resulting diffraction patterns.

entry.title: Superradiant photon bunching in nanolasers: how a hierarchy of polarization orders leads to Dicke Markov chains
entry.summary: Superradiant photon bunching in nanolasers: from a polarization-order hierarchy of the master equation to Dicke Markov chains arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies how a few to several hundred quantum emitters sharing one light mode in nanolasers produce superradiant bursts and strongly bunched photon statistics below threshold. The authors derive a hierarchy of models from the laser master equation, classified by polarization order, and show that eliminating all coherences yields a Dicke Markov chain predicting superthermal bunching and an even-odd dependence on emitter number. A population-polarization model that keeps the optical polarization but eliminates two-photon coherences reproduces the full master equation's bunching almost perfectly.

entry.title: U(1)-Symmetric Spin SYK Models: Ordering, Chaos, and Transport
entry.summary: U(1)-Symmetric Spin SYK Models: Ordering, Chaos, and Transport arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies a U(1)-symmetric spin version of the complex SYK model, built from random charge-conserving multi-spin interactions native to qubit systems, which avoids fermionic encoding overhead. In the large-N, large-q limit, it reproduces the leading saddle-point structure of complex fermionic SYK. Using exact diagonalization at finite size, the authors examine ordering susceptibility, level statistics, and domain-wall dynamics in coupled-cluster chains.

entry.title: Bell nonlocality can be revealed without repeating any measurement direction
entry.summary: Revealing Bell Nonlocality Does Not Require the Same Physical Measurement to be Performed Twice arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper asks whether Bell inequality violations still occur when measurement directions never repeat. The authors ran an experiment with polarization-entangled photons, detecting only one particle pair per randomly chosen analyzer direction. They report that violations remain possible and keep their operational significance even without repeated measurements.

entry.title: Learning Quantum Hamiltonians from Dynamical Structure Factor Data for Neutron Scattering Analysis
entry.summary: Learning Quantum Hamiltonians from the Dynamical Structure Factor arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper studies how to learn a quantum Hamiltonian, which describes microscopic interactions, from the dynamical structure factor (DSF) that captures two-point correlations in quantum magnets. The authors show the DSF contains enough information to efficiently reconstruct broad classes of quantum Hamiltonians. Using simple relations between low-order spectral moments of the DSF and microscopic couplings, they introduce three complementary tomography protocols based on high-temperature expansion, strong-field polarization, and the fluctuation-dissipation theorem. The framework is intended for practical use with common experimental data such as neutron scattering.

entry.title: Crystal-symmetry anomalies in lattice systems and a crystalline equivalence principle
entry.summary: Crystalline Equivalence Principle for Anomalies arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper gives a microscopic description of crystalline symmetry anomalies in bosonic lattice systems in one and two spatial dimensions. The authors construct anomaly indices for symmetry operators and derive their cocycle conditions and coboundary ambiguities. The results establish a crystalline equivalence principle for bosonic anomalies, and show that a nontrivial total anomaly index prevents a symmetric invertible phase. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build microscopic anomaly indices for crystalline symmetries on bosonic lattices, establish a crystalline equivalence principle, and prove obstructions to symmetric invertible phases.

entry.title: Boosting neutral-atom gate fidelity by correlating and synchronizing atomic motion
entry.summary: Enhanced Entanglement Gate Fidelity via Correlated and Synchronized Atom Motion arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies two-qubit controlled-phase gates based on Rydberg blockade in neutral-atom tweezer arrays. It shows that engineered collective dissipation can correlate and synchronize atomic motion, which suppresses motion-induced gate errors. At finite temperature, these motional correlations reduce gate infidelity compared with independent thermal atoms.

entry.title: Buffer-gas-assisted fluorescence spectroscopy of molecular ions
entry.summary: Buffer-Gas-Assisted Fluorescence Spectroscopy of Molecular Ions arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper presents a nondestructive method for continuous fluorescence detection of strongly rovibronically open molecular ions, specifically 232ThF+. Room-temperature buffer-gas collisions replenish the laser-addressed states, creating effective quasi-cycling transitions without optical repumping or auxiliary atomic readout ions. A signal-to-noise ratio of about 6 is reported for the P(1) line in a 1 s exposure.

entry.title: Comparing quantum and classical thermal equilibrium for probabilistic classical fields
entry.summary: Quantum and classical thermal equilibrium for probabilistic classical fields arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper describes how the time evolution of probability distributions for classical fields can be captured by quantum formalism, with free quantum field theory appearing as a subsystem for free fields. It compares the momentum dependence of energy and field correlations under classical (Rayleigh-Jeans) and quantum (Planck) thermal equilibrium. Numerical simulations with interactions are used to determine which equilibrium is selected by asymptotic dynamics. For free fields, the authors construct a classical-quantum map between the classical probability distribution and a quantum field theory density matrix.

entry.title: Critical excited states in quantum metrology: a paper on using phase-transition behavior of excited states to improve precision measurements.
entry.summary: Critical excited states in quantum metrology arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies criticality-enhanced sensing near ground- and excited-state quantum phase transitions in a strongly coupled qubit-boson system. Accounting for finite-size effects, the authors design driving protocols that exploit diverging susceptibilities to boost signal-to-noise ratios in parameter estimation. They show that excited-state criticality offers a metrological advantage through single-mode bosonic squeezing in regimes that avoid the death of adiabaticity.

entry.title: Exact mixed encodings for resource-limited QAOA
entry.summary: Exact Mixed-Locality Encodings for Resource-Constrained QAOA arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper studies how to choose Hamiltonian encodings for higher-order objectives in the quantum approximate optimisation algorithm (QAOA) on resource-constrained hardware. It proposes a family of pointwise-exact mixed representations that replace selected higher-order interactions with shared Rosenberg auxiliaries while keeping the rest native, with conditions certifying exactness. Compilation experiments on 12-qubit line, ring, and grid targets identify feasible mixed-only regions for many instances, while noiseless depth-one evaluation shows the native encoding achieving the best mean objective.

entry.title: Defect-stabilized Wigner negativity and parity-protected phase locking in a quantum oscillator
entry.summary: Defect-induced stabilization of Wigner negativity and parity-protected phase-locking arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper shows that a parity-preserving delta-shaped potential, modeling a localized defect, reduces the continuous U(1) symmetry of a quantum van der Pol oscillator to a discrete Z2 symmetry. This protects even-parity steady-state quantum coherences, producing non-classical steady states with negative Wigner functions. The authors also propose an experiment using the motional states of ultracold alkaline-earth-like atoms in optical tweezers.

entry.title: Detecting single-molecule rotational collisions using quantum logic
entry.summary: Quantum-logic detection of rotationally inelastic collisions of single molecules arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper presents a method for detecting individual rotationally inelastic collisions between single trapped molecular ions and neutral helium atoms. The researchers prepare N2+ ions in their rotational ground state, expose them to a helium beam, and identify collision events from changes in the ions' motion. Quantum-logic spectroscopy reveals the molecular state changes after collisions, and the results are compared with quantum and classical scattering calculations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors detect single rotationally inelastic collisions of trapped N2+ ions with helium using quantum-logic readout, compared against quantum and classical scattering calculations.

entry.title: Quantum non-Gaussian coherence generated by dissipation into single qubits
entry.summary: Quantum non-Gaussian coherence via dissipation to single qubits arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper proposes a way to deterministically generate high-order quantum non-Gaussian coherence in bosonic systems. It alternates pulsed Gaussian control of a linear oscillator with dissipation into a single ground-state qubit via resonant Jaynes-Cummings interactions. The authors report that this produces binary superpositions of low Fock states up to N=4, as well as binomial code states and logical magic states, with fidelities above 0.98.

entry.title: Feedback Control and Neural-Network Prediction of Quantum Entanglement in Fano-Mirror Cavity Optomechanics
entry.summary: Feedback Control and Neural-Network-Based Prediction of Quantum Entanglement in Fano-mirror cavity optomechanics arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper proposes a theoretical scheme using a Fano-mirror cavity optomechanical system with a coherent feedback loop to generate, manipulate, and predict entanglement between a mechanical object and optical modes. Quantum interference between direct and indirect interaction pathways is shown to enhance cavity-mechanical entanglement and produce robust Fano-mechanical entanglement. Coherent feedback combined with an optical frequency mismatch further strengthens the entanglement, and a trained feedforward neural network can predict its magnitude from readily measurable optical signals.

entry.title: A max-flow min-cut theorem for quantum graphs
entry.summary: A Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem for Quantum Graphs arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper proposes definitions of cuts and flows for quantum graphs, including ordinary cuts that split the vertex set into two parts and generalised cuts defined as a continuous relaxation of the binary partition function. It proves that the maximum S-T flow in a quantum graph equals the minimum generalised S-T cut for any disjoint terminal sets S and T. The minimum ordinary cut can be larger. For classical graphs, both minima coincide, recovering the classical theorem.

entry.title: Restoring Heisenberg scaling in Hamiltonian estimation under noise uncertainty
entry.summary: Restoring Heisenberg Scaling in Hamiltonian Estimation despite Noise Uncertainty arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies how uncertainty about noise parameters affects the precision of estimating Hamiltonian parameters in quantum sensors. For general Markovian dynamics under arbitrary quantum control, it derives a necessary and sufficient condition for each Hamiltonian parameter to keep Heisenberg scaling and gives its optimal asymptotic precision when the condition holds. When the condition fails, the authors propose a protocol using a noisy reference system to restore this scaling. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive a necessary and sufficient condition for Heisenberg scaling under unknown Markovian noise and propose a noisy reference protocol restoring optimal precision.

entry.title: Time evolution of a dipolar XY magnet, modeled with cumulant equations
entry.summary: Cumulant dynamics of the ferromagnetic dipolar XY model arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies how a dipolar ferromagnetic XY model on a square lattice evolves when its parameters are changed, using second-order truncated cumulant dynamics for systems up to linear size 60. The results show that a coherent region of finite size and finite magnetization can form even under diabatic but sufficiently slow ramps. These two scales depend on the ramp constant, the initial entropy, and time. The authors note that their findings place strong requirements on future experiments aiming at dipolar XY equilibrium physics in larger systems.

entry.title: Infrared vacuum lowers the laser energy needed to break chemical bonds in simple molecules
entry.summary: The infrared vacuum reduces the laser energy needed to break molecular bonds of simple molecules arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies infrared photodissociation of a single molecule strongly coupled to a resonant infrared nanocavity mode. A monochromatic laser either vibrationally excites the molecule directly or injects photons into the nanocavity field. The authors compare CO2 and H2O dynamics inside the cavity and find that dissociation requires up to three orders of magnitude less driving energy when photons are injected into the nanocavity than when the molecule is driven directly. The enhancement is attributed to the interplay of nuclear anharmonicity, strong light-matter coupling, and vacuum field polarisation according to the dipolar nature of the molecular bond.

entry.title: Work extractable from quantum batteries charged via collective dark states
entry.summary: Extractable Work from Collective Dark-State Charging of Quantum Batteries arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies two groups of superconducting qubits, one acting as a charger and the other as a battery, both coupled to a shared lossy resonator. Destructive interference between their collective decay amplitudes selects a tunable family of dark states, enabling controlled energy transfer from charger to battery. The authors report that the battery's passive energy stays below the single-qubit excitation energy ω0 regardless of battery size. For a fixed nonzero average stored energy per qubit, total stored energy grows linearly with the number of qubits N, and the ratio of global ergotropy to stored energy approaches one as N increases.

entry.title: Large-scale mapping of silicon T centres using tuning-free broadband cavities
entry.summary: Large-scale characterisation of silicon T centres with tuning-free broadband cavities arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies T centres in silicon, defects that emit in the telecom O-band and host long-lived electron and nuclear spins. The authors fabricated an array of 400 low-quality-factor confocal cavities that align with the T centre wavelength without individual tuning. The array increases the median T centre signal 6.5-fold, speeding measurements by 42 times. Comparing cavity statistics with a Monte Carlo simulation, the authors infer a T centre density of 4.2^{+1.3}_{-0.8} μm⁻² without relying on the setup's collection efficiency.

entry.title: Entanglement spreading after quenches from highly entangled states
entry.summary: Going beyond the standard quasiparticle picture: Entanglement spreading after quenching from highly entangled states arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies how entanglement entropy spreads after quantum quenches in the XXZ spin chain, starting from n-rainbow states built from increasingly long-range Bell pairs. In the interacting XXZ chain, tDMRG simulations show that entropy grows at the rate thermodynamic entropy is exchanged across the cut. In the noninteracting XX chain, the quench creates entangled multiplets of 2n quasiparticle species, and a generalized quasiparticle picture captures the suppression of entanglement growth. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend the quasiparticle picture to n-rainbow initial states, combining analytic results for XX chains with tDMRG simulations of the interacting XXZ chain.

entry.title: Quantum Euclid algorithm and its use in factoring
entry.summary: The Quantum Euclid Algorithm and its Application to Factoring arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper presents a quantum implementation of the Euclid algorithm for computing the greatest common divisor when one integer is a product of two odd primes. It discusses applying this to quantum factoring, where modular exponentiation is not needed and factors are revealed directly by measurement. The authors note that the method does not scale favourably to large numbers.

entry.title: A unified benchmark comparing circuit designs for quantum chemistry calculations on near-term quantum computers
entry.summary: A Unified Benchmarking Study of Variational Quantum Eigensolver Ansatz for Electronic Structure Problems arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper systematically compares four circuit designs (ansatze) for the Variational Quantum Eigensolver on molecules H₂, LiH, and N₂: UCCSD, fermionic ADAPT-VQE, and two hardware-efficient ansatze. It evaluates circuit depth, parameter count, ground-state energy error, and feasibility on NISQ devices.
