ADAPT-VQE reaches accuracy close to UCCSD with lower resource overhead but becomes impractical at around 10 electrons. Hardware-efficient ansatze reduce hardware costs but need more parameters and are less accurate.

entry.title: When Quantum Correlations Matter for Quantum Annealing
entry.summary: When Do Quantum Correlations Matter for Quantum Annealing? arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper compares quantum annealing (QA) with quantum-inspired annealing (QIA), a classical method that keeps QA's Hamiltonian structure and annealing schedule but excludes nonlocal quantum correlations. Across models differing in dimensionality, disorder, and frustration, the scaling difference between the two depends strongly on the model. QA has a clear advantage in clean, low-dimensional systems, which shrinks as dimensionality grows and becomes negligible in three or more dimensions. Disorder and frustration narrow the gap further.

entry.title: Quantization Breaks Classical Mpemba Constraints
entry.summary: Quantization Breaks Classical Mpemba Constraints arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper starts from the Caldeira-Leggett model and establishes a correspondence between quantum and classical thermal relaxation. It finds that the locality of classical energy diffusion forbids the Mpemba effect in single-well and symmetric double-well potentials. Quantum dynamics, by allowing direct transitions between nonadjacent energy levels, enables the effect in these potentials, while in the semiclassical limit the classical constraints are restored.

entry.title: Domain of the effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian in quantum Markovian dynamics
entry.summary: On the domain of the effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian in quantum markovian dynamics arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies how the domains of three operators relate in the unbounded generator of a quantum Markov semigroup, where one part is a negative self-adjoint operator and the other is a symmetric operator. The authors show that the generator's domain equals the intersection of the two individual domains when both parts are self-adjoint quadratic polynomials in annihilation and creation operators on a finite-mode bosonic Fock space, under either a sign condition or a half-bound on their commutator. A counterexample shows the conclusion fails in general.

entry.title: Cumulants of operator semigroups for many-particle evolution equation hierarchies
entry.summary: Cumulants of Operator Semigroups for Hierarchies of Many-Particle Evolution Equations arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper gives a brief overview of recent mathematical advances on evolution equations for quantum many-particle systems. It outlines expansions that represent non-perturbative solutions to the Cauchy problem for these hierarchies. The authors show that the cumulants of operator semigroups underpin these representations, and that the constructed correlation dynamics describe state evolution for both finite and infinite particle numbers.

entry.title: Device-independent tests for genuine multipartite entanglement and nonlocality in GHZ states and Bell-pair trees
entry.summary: Device-independent witnesses of genuine multipartite entanglement and nonlocality for GHZ states and Bell-pair tree arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper derives and compares device-independent witnesses for genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) and genuine multipartite nonlocality (GMNL) in GHZ states and trees of Bell pairs. It presents a binary-outcome family using four global measurement contexts whose tight biseparable bound does not depend on the number of parties, and a 2N-context GMNL witness for GHZ states compared with MABK and Svetlichny tests. For Bell-pair trees, sums of CHSH and chained inequalities certify GME and GMNL respectively. The authors also benchmark these witnesses on IBM Quantum GHZ preparations with up to 10 parties. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a four-context binary-outcome GME witness with a tight party-independent biseparable bound and benchmark it on IBM Quantum GHZ states.

entry.title: Trading memory for depth: tight bounds for LCU block-encodings
entry.summary: Trading Memory for Depth: Tight Bounds for LCU Block-Encodings arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies the select depth of linear combination of unitaries (LCU) block-encodings. Grouping the terms into g parallel registers yields a depth bound set by the binning makespan and the largest bin, and the authors show a two-way reduction to classical multiprocessor scheduling so that an optimal binning attains the bound. The paper also compares two selector realisations that trade space against depth. ★★★★ Notable: The authors reduce LCU block-encoding select depth to multiprocessor scheduling in both directions, giving tight bounds and a memory-depth tradeoff.

entry.title: A master equation for open quantum systems with nonlinear system-bath coupling
entry.summary: Dissipaton-embedded quantum master equation for nonlinear system-bath coupling arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper presents a dissipaton-embedded quantum master equation for nonlinear coupling between a system and its bath. The dissipaton theory, first proposed as a statistical quasiparticle theory for open quantum systems, was later extended to nonlinear coupling, and its rigorous mathematical foundation was only recently established. Building on this, the authors formulate a master equation that is exact in principle and describes the joint dynamics of the reduced system and all dissipaton degrees of freedom.

entry.title: A real-time error-correction system for neutral-atom quantum computers
entry.summary: An Architecture for Real-Time Quantum Error Correction with Neutral Atoms arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper presents a heterogeneous architecture for neutral-atom quantum processors that overlaps fluorescence readout with classical decoding at two spatial scales. FPGAs process camera rows as they arrive, while GPUs decode a completed logical block during acquisition of the next. Benchmarks using circuit-level simulated syndromes report post-exposure processing latency below one millisecond for small codes with distances 3, 5, and 7.

entry.title: One molecule, many outputs: exact diagnostics for quantum circuits encoding molecules by atom
entry.summary: One molecule, many outputs; many molecules, one output: exact diagnostics for atom-level compositional quantum encoders arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper adapts quantum natural language processing to molecules, treating each heavy atom as a word and each bond as a wire so the circuit wiring follows the molecular graph. With typed angle sharing the circuits separate every tested isomer pair, but for pairs that simpler sharing confuses, output states stay nearly identical before and after training, with differences mostly in measurement success probability. The authors explain this through a bond-based graph model, note that SMILES writing order can change outputs, and claim no quantum advantage over a simple atom-count baseline.

entry.title: Compiling Efficient Tapers for Reliable Quantum Phase Estimation
entry.summary: Scalable Compilation of Resource-Efficient Tapers for High-Confidence Quantum Phase Estimation arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies tapered quantum phase estimation (tQPE), which greatly lowers failure probability while needing few extra ancilla qubits. The authors use tensor network methods to build scalable state preparation circuits for optimally concentrated DPSS (Slepian) tapers and release a database covering l = 1 to 50 and m = 1 to 4. Experiments on Quantinuum's H2-2 computer with a one-qubit system show a 3 to 18 times reduction in failure probability for l = 1 to 10.

entry.title: Entanglement and correlations in light-to-medium nuclei for symmetry-adapted quantum simulation
entry.summary: Entanglement, correlations, and resource costs for symmetry-adapted quantum simulations of light through medium-mass nuclei arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper uses nuclear symmetries to study entanglement and correlations in ab initio symmetry-adapted no-core shell-model wavefunctions for nuclei including He-4, He-6, He-8, Be-8, C-12, Ne-20 and Ca-48. It computes single-mode entropies and two-mode mutual information, and examines how like-particle pair correlations organize into symmetry channels. The dominant pair correlations are captured by fewer SU(3) channels than angular-momentum channels, and a Fiedler-based register ordering reduces ordering cost.

entry.title: Detecting frequencies with one qubit at the discrete Grover-Heisenberg limit
entry.summary: Sensing frequencies at the discrete Grover-Heisenberg limit using a single qubit arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies a quantum sensing task: detecting weak oscillating fields whose strength and frequency are unknown. Prior work set a lower bound on the required sensing time, the Grover-Heisenberg limit, using a protocol that needs auxiliary qubits. The authors show that a single sensing qubit suffices for a discrete version where the signal strength is known and the frequency is drawn from a known finite set of candidates. Its sensing time grows only with the square root of the number of candidates, and this dependence is proven optimal in the worst case. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show a single qubit achieves square-root scaling in candidate frequencies and prove worst-case optimality for the discrete problem.

entry.title: A learning-based method for measuring qubit energy-level leakage precisely.
entry.summary: High-precision measurement of level leakage via intelligent coherent control arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper addresses level leakage, a major error source in quantum control, by proposing a reinforcement learning-based quantum sensing algorithm for estimating it with high precision. It studies both Hermitian three-level systems and effective dissipative two-level systems using experimentally feasible pulse-parameter modulation. Pulse sequences discovered by a DQN improve sensing precision, and joint phase-detuning modulation further raises performance so that the classical Fisher information (CFI) approaches the quantum Fisher information (QFI).

entry.title: Lowering TLS Losses in Superconducting Circuits with Solid Neon
entry.summary: Reducing TLS Losses in Superconducting Circuits Using Solid Neon arXiv · Nov 11, 2026Two-level systems (TLSs) are a major loss source in superconducting devices. Using NbTiN coplanar waveguide resonators, the authors show that depositing and then removing a solid neon film significantly improves device performance. Temperature and power dependence analysis attributes the gain to reduced TLS dissipation, linked to redistribution and removal of surface contaminants during neon deposition and evaporation.

entry.title: Fastest and Photon-Minimal Paths for Preparing and Flipping GKP States
entry.summary: Time- and Photon-Optimal Paths for the Preparation and Logical Flip of Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill States arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies how to prepare Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) states and perform logical gates on them. The authors use the brachistochrone, the fastest path at bounded speed, to build ideal nonlinear Hamiltonians and compare it with the photon-optimal path. The two paths nearly coincide for state preparation but differ clearly for logical bit flips. The authors also introduce a tangential capacity to measure how well gate sets follow these paths, and find that conditional squeezing performs best, preparing GKP states in 824 ns with fidelity 0.99.

entry.title: From optimization to construction: expanding quantum measurement designs
entry.summary: From optimization to construction: Expanding quantum measurement designs arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper addresses the sampling cost of estimating molecular energies on quantum computers, which requires repeated measurements of many Pauli terms. It introduces variance-guided measurement group construction (VGMC), which changes which Hamiltonian terms share measurement shots and jointly optimizes estimator coefficients and shot allocations. On molecular benchmarks with exact covariances, VGMC reduced variance by 18.19% to 23.38% compared with state-of-the-art measurement design methods.

entry.title: Epitaxial nitride junctions with crystalline barriers for superconducting circuits
entry.summary: Nitride crystalline barrier epitaxial SIS Josephson junctions by MBE arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper reports Josephson junctions with a crystalline AlN tunnel barrier, grown by molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) in NbN/AlN/NbN trilayers. The barrier is about 4.5 nm thick, and the devices show coherent Josephson tunneling with a critical current density of about 17 A/cm². Hysteretic current-voltage curves and Fraunhofer modulation in magnetic field confirm underdamped SIS junction behavior. The authors suggest the approach could enable alloy and superlattice electrodes and barriers, and monolithic integration with devices such as HEMTs and lasers.

entry.title: Local enhancement for reliable quantum code preparation at finite measurement strength
entry.summary: Local enhancement of finite-strength code preparation: recoverability and Wilson coherence arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper studies preparing quantum error-correcting codes with finite-strength stabilizer measurements, which deform the encoding away from the ideal projective limit. It shows that at fixed strength, local logical leakage prevents asymptotically faithful recovery, and that enhancing only a vanishing fraction of checks near logical supports restores recoverability while the bulk stays at finite strength. The authors further find that in the three-dimensional deconfined phase, enhanced tubes restore equivalence of macroscopically separated logical representatives, whereas in two dimensions recoverability alone does not. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show local enhancement of finite-strength measurements restores recoverability, and report a dimensional distinction in logical operations between three and two dimensions. Impact is mainl

entry.title: CSS circuits: practical quantum circuits simulable at O(1) cost per gate
entry.summary: CSS Circuits: useful quantum circuits that can be simulated with O(1) cost per gate arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies CSS circuits, quantum circuits built only from X, Z, measurement (M_X, M_Z), and CNOT gates. Despite these strict restrictions, they can implement important protocols such as teleportation, error correction, and entanglement purification. The authors present a simple CSS circuit simulator that uses O(1) work per gate. Using Bell inequalities, they prove the simulator cannot also support Hadamard, CZ, or S gates. The paper notes that CSS circuits are well suited for benchmarking quantum error correction under atom loss errors.

entry.title: Quantum CSS codes: decoder-aware multiobjective design and bound-certified selection
entry.summary: Quantum CSS codes: Decoder-aware multiobjective design and bound-certified selection arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies quantum error-correcting codes, weighing decoding reliability against the resources needed to measure their checks. It formulates CSS code design as a multiobjective problem that considers failure probability under sector-wise degenerate maximum-likelihood decoding and check weight. Deterministic truncation bounds support selecting codes under a failure-rate constraint. In paired searches, decoder-aware guidance achieved significantly higher mean final hypervolume than distance guidance in all eight tested configurations.

entry.title: Comparing quantum circuit protection methods after compilation
entry.summary: Evaluating Quantum Circuit Protection Methods After Compilation: An Empirical Comparison arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper compares three ObfusQate schemes (inverse, composite and delayed gates), ECQCO and Q-MaskCut, all compiled at optimisation level 3 before measurement. Composite and delayed gates lose most of their structural disguise during compilation, leaving the output readable. Inverse gates keep a high normalised graph edit distance but run 7 to 112 times longer. Q-MaskCut hides the output but needs 7 to 91 fragment variants per circuit and classical reconstruction. The authors argue protection should be evaluated after compilation and after recompilation by the provider.

entry.title: Using large language models to generate quantum circuit parameters
entry.summary: Programming Quantum Circuit Parameters with Large Language Models arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper studies whether a frozen, general-purpose large language model can generate complete parameter vectors for variational quantum circuits from symbolic circuit and Hamiltonian descriptions, with optional iterative energy feedback. It tests random Hamiltonians, structured parent Hamiltonians, and molecular systems. For general Hamiltonians the generated parameters show larger energy errors than Adam optimization, while for structured Hamiltonians the model can produce promising low-energy configurations.

entry.title: Quantum machine learning that expresses uncertainty using Dempster-Shafer theory
entry.summary: Uncertainty-aware quantum machine learning based on Dempster-Shafer theory arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper introduces a quantum classification framework that represents prediction uncertainty using Dempster-Shafer theory, assigning weights to individual labels and to sets of labels. The authors propose a training strategy that lets parameterized quantum circuits learn these weight assignments directly from data. The approach supports quantum Dempster-Shafer fusion with polynomial resource requirements.

entry.title: Key Relay vs. Secure Network Coding: One-Shot Equivalence and Separation on Undirected Networks
entry.summary: Key Relay and Secure Network Coding: One-Shot Equivalence and Separation on Undirected Networks arXiv · Nov 12, 2026Motivated by quantum key distribution networks, this paper compares key relay protocols with secure network coding on the same undirected graph. For two terminals and a one-symbol key, arbitrary key relay is shown to be equivalent to scalar linear acyclic network coding, but this equivalence fails in general when several terminals seek one common key. A four-terminal complete graph example over a ternary field separates the two approaches, and the paper also establishes a linear key relay normal form.

entry.title: Exact quantum algorithms for composed Boolean functions
entry.summary: Exact Quantum Algorithms for Composed Boolean Functions arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper studies exact quantum algorithms for block compositions of total Boolean functions and proves an upper bound on exact quantum query complexity in terms of the outer function's exact query complexity and polynomial degree. Applied to recursive ternary not-all-equal and other fixed gadgets, it yields improved exact rates. The composition technique also transfers separations from approximate query complexity and degree to exact quantum query complexity. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a composition construction whose costs are governed by exact query complexity and degree, improving separation exponents.

entry.title: Scaling Pelagos: Multi-GPU Software for Faster Quantum Error-Correction Decoding
entry.summary: Scaling Pêlagos: Multi-GPU Orchestration for Relay Belief-Propagation Decoding arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper extends the Pelagos relay belief-propagation (Relay-BP) decoder, a tool for correcting errors in quantum computers, so it runs across multiple GPUs. The changes add process-isolated orchestration, parallel host preprocessing, and shared-memory output to reduce overhead. Tests on two codes, the one-gross and two-gross codes, report end-to-end speedups of about 5.68 to 7.01 times. The system has been deployed on Oak Ridge National Laboratory's Lux supercomputer.

entry.title: Hierarchical decoding for quantum error correction: a review of algorithms, code designs, and hardware trade-offs
entry.summary: Hierarchical Decoding for Quantum Error Correction arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper reviews hierarchical decoding for quantum error correction, covering single-code approaches such as cascaded predecoding and windowed, streaming, and distributed implementations. It also examines how decoding is coordinated across levels of hierarchical and concatenated codes, how qubit modalities affect decoding workloads and timing, and how CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs, ASICs, and cryogenic platforms meet these requirements. The authors identify gaps in performance reporting and system integration.

entry.title: TGen-SQD: A Physics-Informed Transferable Configuration Generator for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization
entry.summary: TGen-SQD: Physics-Informed Transferable Configuration Generator for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization arXiv · Nov 12, 2026Sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) estimates a molecule's ground-state energy by selecting a compact subset of determinants. TGen-SQD is a generator trained jointly across multiple Hamiltonians, using configuration-interaction-weighted data and orbital- and system-level descriptors to guide selection. Its weights stay frozen after training and are applied to both seen and zero-shot geometries. On a 20-qubit H10 chain, it achieves mean energy errors of 40.18 ± 1.52 and 43.97 ± 1.20 mHa, 12.7% and 11.7% lower than the PIGen-SQD baseline under matched budgets.

entry.title: Quasi-cyclic qudit lifted product codes with near-linear minimum distance
entry.summary: Quasi-Cyclic Qudit Lifted Product Codes with Almost Linear Minimum Distance arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper introduces a qudit generalization of the lifted product construction over cyclic group algebras, extending it to arbitrary prime-power dimensions and yielding quasi-cyclic qudit CSS codes. In the fully stacked case, families built from lifted Tanner codes on expander graphs have Θ(log N) logical qudits and almost linear minimum distance Θ(N/log N). Monte Carlo simulations under a depolarizing channel show that the qudit codes achieve lower frame error rates than comparable qubit codes, with a linear merged-syndrome decoder giving further gains.

entry.title: k-partite quantum homomorphisms: a framework for multiplayer quantum constraint problems
entry.summary: k-partite quantum homomorphisms arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper extends k-XOR games to k-partite homomorphism games on arbitrary relational structures, providing a framework for multipartite quantum constraint satisfaction and quantum homomorphisms. It characterises perfect strategies in the tensor-product and commuting-operator models as Kleisli morphisms of graded quantum monads. The authors compare synchronous and k-partite quantum advantage, exhibit an NP-complete six-element template with two-player quantum advantage, and prove that no bounded-width template admits k-partite quantum advantage.

entry.title: Quantum search methods for finding paths that meet several metric limits at once
entry.summary: On Multi-Constrained Path Finding utilizing Grover Search and Decoded Quantum Interferometry arXiv · Nov 12, 2026The paper studies finding a path in a directed acyclic graph whose totals under several additive metrics all fall within given ranges. The authors propose a Grover search whose state preparation builds a uniform superposition over all source-to-destination paths using one qubit per arc and no ancilla, and they prove its correctness and give its exact gate count. They relate the problem to max-LINSAT and Optimal Polynomial Intersection, verify the translation in simulation, and run two small binary instances on IBM Heron processors.

entry.title: Subadditivity and failure of strong subadditivity in Nichols–Wootters entropies
entry.summary: Subadditivity and the failure of strong subadditivity in the Nichols--Wootters family of entropies arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper proves subadditivity for the Nichols–Wootters family of entropies, which interpolates between the von Neumann entropy and the subentropy, with all spectra computed in a common ambient dimension. Except for the von Neumann entropy, equality holds exactly when at least one marginal is pure, settling a conjecture on subentropy. Every member other than the von Neumann entropy fails strong subadditivity, already for a maximally entangled two-qubit state tensored with a mixed qubit. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove subadditivity for the Nichols-Wootters entropy family and characterize the failure of strong subadditivity, with tight bounds and a channel-capacity application.

entry.title: Hybrid classical-quantum optimization for time-window vehicle routing, with feasibility guarantees and hardware limits
entry.summary: Hybrid Classical-Quantum Optimization for CVRPTW: A Systems Framework with Provable Feasibility and Empirical Hardware Limits arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper presents a hybrid architecture that combines mixed integer linear programming with vehicle-level quadratic unconstrained binary optimization to solve capacitated vehicle routing problems with time windows. It runs the subproblems on Toshiba SQBM+ and on QAOA using Rigetti Ankaa-3 and IQM Emerald quantum processors, and evaluates five benchmarks derived from London traffic and location data. SQBM+ reduced fleet distance by 2.80% (7,927 m) on a 25-customer instance and 0.22% (1,186 m) on a 55-customer instance. QAOA experiments show reliable constraint satisfaction on current hardware only for subproblems of up to 4 customers (16 qubits).

entry.title: Quantum recurrent networks for financial forecasting: a hybrid-model comparison study
entry.summary: Quantum Recurrent Architectures for Financial Time Series Prediction arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper evaluates quantum-classical hybrid recurrent models, a Quantum LSTM and quantum reservoir computing with lag-based inputs, for forecasting financial time series. Using a monthly revenue series extended to 1056 months, the models are compared against full-size and parameter-matched classical LSTMs, classical reservoir computing, and SARIMA over ten seeds. The authors find no evidence of a quantum advantage in accuracy or parameter efficiency in this low-dimensional setting.

entry.title: Multi-head quantum neural networks replacing transformer blocks in a 30-billion-parameter LLM
entry.summary: Multi-head Quantum Neural Networks: Replacing Transformer Blocks with NISQ Modules inside a 30-Billion-Parameter LLM arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper introduces a multi-head quantum neural network (QNN) that splits hidden neurons into heads, processes each with a quantum circuit, and couples them through classical linear layers. The authors replace a span of eight transformer blocks in Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 with one module of 145,281 trainable parameters. The quantum heads were executed on a 156-qubit IBM Heron processor.

entry.title: Structure-aware checking of whether two quantum circuits are equivalent, using sparse Pauli propagation
entry.summary: Structure-Aware Quantum Circuit Equivalence Checking via Sparse Pauli Propagation arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper presents a method for checking whether two unitary quantum circuits are equivalent, based on sparse Pauli propagation. It combines two complementary strategies, generator propagation and Cut-Miter, and selects between them according to circuit structure. On two benchmark suites with circuit pairs of up to 512 qubits, the method matched reference verdicts for 96.3% of pairs with no incorrect verdicts and cut total runtime by 48.5% to 76.0% relative to the baselines.

entry.title: QSim-Arena: An Evolving Framework for Assessing Quantum Simulation Advantage
entry.summary: QSim-Arena: an evolving developer for quantum simulation advantage arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper presents QSim-Arena, a research framework in which AI agents run a closed loop of verification and benchmarking alongside open exploration. The agents reproduce published simulation techniques and compare their performance across diverse Hamiltonian families, using independently cross-checked classical methods as baselines. Initial applications improved baseline quantum resource estimates by integrating established techniques.

entry.title: Quantum simulation of damped sound and elastic waves with absorbing boundaries and compact quantum circuits
entry.summary: Quantum simulation of dissipative acoustic and elastic waves by Schrödingerization: absorbing boundaries and explicit polynomial-size circuits arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper simulates acoustic and elastic wave equations on a quantum computer while opening the domain with a graded sponge layer that damps waves near the outer edge. It uses Schrödingerisation to convert the non-unitary damped evolution into unitary evolutions via one auxiliary variable, deriving the full chain from partial differential equation to circuit in one, two and three dimensions. The authors report that damping all wave fields absorbs better than velocity-only damping, and that the damping step factorises exactly into polynomially many multi-controlled phase gates. Gate-level simulations on up to 25 qubits agree with classical solutions of the damped wave equations.

entry.title: Quantum Krylov sampling solver for elliptic problems with energy-norm error guarantees
entry.summary: Sample-Based Quantum Krylov Galerkin Solvers for Elliptic Partial Differential Equations on Curved Geometries with Hardware Validation arXiv · Oct 11, 2026This paper studies a sample-based quantum linear solver that measures quantum Krylov states and reconstructs the solution of positive-definite systems from elliptic PDEs using a Galerkin solve on the sampled set. It derives energy-norm error bounds, a sample complexity result, and a computable residual certificate. The method is applied to pulsatile flow in elliptic, lens-shaped, and curved ducts, with simulations of up to 12 qubits and measurements on a six-qubit trapped-ion processor. A classical residual-greedy selection is reported to outperform quantum sampling in all cases studied.

entry.title: Can system dynamics stay non-Markovian when measurable memory effects vanish?
entry.summary: Under what conditions can coupling disorder render qubit dynamics CP-divisible in a finite spin bath? arXiv · Oct 14, 2026The study examines how unresolved quasistatic disorder in system-bath coupling affects non-Markovian dynamics in spin environments. For pure dephasing Ising interactions with fixed bath states, disorder can make dynamics CP-divisible, but physically fluctuating bath states keep the averaged dynamics CP-indivisible at any finite disorder. Anisotropic Heisenberg interactions with any nonzero transverse exchange prevent this disorder-driven transition. Increasing disorder suppresses experimentally visible memory revivals, which can become unresolvable at finite measurement resolution.

entry.title: The memory cost of preparing quantum states one at a time
entry.summary: The memory cost of sequential quantum state preparation arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper asks how much memory a quantum device needs to prepare quantum systems sequentially, one after another. Using quantum resource theories, it compares sequential preparation with collective preparation and shows that both have the same asymptotic memory cost per output under general assumptions. However, sequential preparation can require unboundedly more memory, and this gap is analyzed under energy-conserving and noisy operations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize sequential state preparation memory costs via resource theories, relating them to collective preparation, energy-conserving tight dimensions, and quantum catalysis.

entry.title: Circuit-aware protection against burst errors in lattice surgery
entry.summary: Circuit-aware protection against burst errors in lattice surgery arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies how to protect superconducting qubits during lattice surgery, a method for logical operations, against burst errors caused by high-energy impacts. The authors compare three static protection layouts for a simulated lattice-surgery CNOT, matching the number of protected ancillas and check-type splits. At distance 9, protecting the check type measured during each merge reduces burst-induced excess risk compared with a deep geometric band. At distance 13, this advantage is not resolved under oracle decoding.

entry.title: Quantum Telatar formula: quantum capacity of random multimode fading channels
entry.summary: Quantum Telatar formula: fading quantum capacity of Haar-random multimode attenuators arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper studies unassisted quantum information transmission through Haar-random passive bosonic networks, where the sender does not know the exact channel. It proves that under stated conditions, the zero-temperature quantum capacity grows linearly with the number of modes, mirroring the classical multi-antenna result. At nonzero temperature, a lower bound on capacity is given, and numerical results identify positive achievable rates for cryogenic microwave and room-temperature multimode fiber models. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend Telatar's classical fading capacity result to the quantum case, reporting linear scaling of unassisted quantum capacity in Haar-random bosonic networks with numerical checks.

entry.title: Higher-order exceptional point sensing using Rydberg atom microensemble arrays
entry.summary: Higher-Order Exceptional Point Sensing with Rydberg Micro-Ensemble Arrays arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper builds spatially structured microensemble arrays in cold Rydberg gas, where long-range interactions and spatial connectivity enlarge the effective non-Hermitian dimensionality to realize higher-order exceptional points. Varying the spatial arrangement of the sites yields different orders of these points, and interactions between Rydberg excitation sites are shown to enhance the quantum Fisher information. By tracking shifts of the phase boundaries, the authors report a sensitivity of 0.47(10) nV cm-1 Hz-1/2, surpassing the standard quantum limit.

entry.title: Quantum fluctuations of stress-energy via Noether's theorem and the cosmological constant
entry.summary: Quantum Fluctuations of the Stress-Energy Tensor via Noether's Theorem and the Connection to the Cosmological Constant arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper derives quantum fluctuations of the Noether current directly from Noether's theorem, arising because quantum particles need not follow classical paths. Using spacetime translational symmetry of a complex scalar field, it computes the resulting fluctuations of the stress-energy tensor. Since this tensor sources Einstein's equations, the fluctuations are interpreted as a contribution to the cosmological constant. The result is proportional to the field mass to the fourth power, consistent with earlier expressions.

entry.title: Controlling the Vacuum: Tunable Magnonic Casimir Effect in Magnetic Moiré Systems
entry.summary: Controlling the Vacuum: Tunable Magnonic Casimir Effect in Magnetic Moiré Systems arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper shows that quantum fluctuations of magnetic degrees of freedom in moiré structures can be tuned by adjusting the moiré lattice. Using the Bistritzer-MacDonald approach, the authors show that magnonic vacuum energy and magnonic Casimir force depend on moiré pattern parameters. The calculations use the moiré Ladder as an example and are said to generalize to any moiré structure.

entry.title: Zeroth persistent homology of ground-state correlations at quantum phase transitions
entry.summary: Zeroth persistent homology of ground-state correlations at clean and disordered quantum transitions arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies the antiferromagnetic Ising chain in transverse and longitudinal fields, using exact free-fermion solutions and the density-matrix renormalization group. It applies zeroth persistent homology to staggered ground-state correlations, using the maximum of the persistence-landscape velocity to define a threshold-free pseudocritical point. This point locates the clean critical point and the mixed-order line with accuracy comparable to conventional responses. For individual disordered realizations, the method recovers most strong-disorder renormalization-group clusters.

entry.title: Limiting Free Choice by Embedding Bell Tests in Causal Networks
entry.summary: Bounding Freedom of Choice via Causal Network Embeddings arXiv · Nov 11, 2026Standard Bell inequalities assume measurement independence, meaning measurement settings are fully decoupled from the source of correlations. The paper embeds Bell scenarios into larger causal networks, yielding experimentally accessible lower and upper bounds on measurement dependence whose incompatibility certifies nonclassicality directly from data without assuming free choice. The authors also present a linear-programming framework for systematically deriving these measurement-dependence consistency (MDC) Bell inequalities.

entry.title: Faithful filtering of constrained quantum records: local limits and loop-based joint advantage
entry.summary: Faithful filtering of constrained quantum records: Local limits and collective advantage from loops arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper studies weak probes that record whether neighboring spins are aligned without revealing their common orientation, so that reading them heralds a projection of an unknown spin state onto the aligned subspace while preserving coherences within it. The authors derive the exact optimal success probability over all separable measurements, which equals all local operations with classical communication. They show that joint readout can beat every local strategy for pairwise parity records on a connected simple graph exactly when the graph contains a loop.

entry.title: Quantum synchronization in XX chains under relaxation
entry.summary: Quantum synchronization in XX chains under relaxation arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies stable synchronization of qubit XX chains with site-dependent frequencies and couplings under multi-local amplitude damping noise. It extends earlier results for uniform chains and identifies a spectral matching condition under which edge qubits synchronize. The authors also compute asymptotic pairwise concurrence and show that synchronized pairs stay entangled with a nonzero, constant value in the single-dark-mode case.

entry.title: A Grover-based quantum speedup for searching dark matter
entry.summary: A Grover-Accelerated Search for Dark Matter arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper shows that Grover's algorithm can speed up searches for wave-like dark matter. Dark matter can imprint a coherent phase on a sensor, acting as a repeatable quantum phase gate. Transferring this phase to a qubit register allows a search over N_bins frequency bins to be sped up by a factor of √N_bins.

entry.title: Quantum computing boosts search for wave-like dark matter
entry.summary: Quantum Computing Enhanced Search for Wavelike Dark Matter arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper addresses the challenge of finding weak, random dark matter signals spread across a broad frequency band, using a quantum sensing method based on Grover's search algorithm. The authors show that long integration times stabilize the accumulated sensing phase and reduce errors from dark matter fluctuations, and they alternate the signs of quantum signal processing angles between oracle calls to suppress accumulated approximation errors. In a transmon-based benchmark, the projected sensitivity to axion dark matter exceeds existing astrophysical limits.

entry.title: Toward Distributed Quantum Computing: Gate Teleportation via Satellite-Distributed Entanglement Under Atmospheric Noise
entry.summary: Towards Distributed Quantum Computing: Quantum Gate Teleportation via Satellite-Distributed Entanglement under Atmospheric Depolarization arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies quantum gate teleportation as a building block for satellite-based distributed quantum computing. A satellite sends entangled photon pairs to two ground stations, which deliver this shared resource to remote processors to perform a nonlocal CNOT gate between qubits in different locations. The authors model atmospheric effects as an effective two-qubit depolarizing channel and define a minimal four-qubit protocol. They find that the gate's fidelity depends mainly on the quality of the distributed entanglement, which in turn relies on atmospheric coherence, receiver aperture size, and depolarization strength.

entry.title: Generating squeezed light through Cooper pair recombination in a superconductor-semiconductor device
entry.summary: Squeezed Light Generation by Cooper Pair Recombination in a Superconductor-Semiconductor Structure arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper theoretically proposes a compact, electrically driven device that produces squeezed light using Cooper pair recombination in a hybrid superconductor-semiconductor structure. The authors derive an effective Hamiltonian from second-order perturbation theory to describe how this recombination squeezes the quadrature of the photonic state. They report that squeezing strength scales with the superconducting energy gap squared and device length, and increases with applied voltage.

entry.title: Probing Krylov Dynamics in Driven Many-Body Systems: Exact solutions for operator-growth complexity under time-dependent Hamiltonians in quantum gases and spin systems
entry.summary: Probing Krylov Dynamics in Driven Many-Body Systems arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper solves the time-dependent many-body Krylov problem exactly and in closed form for scale- and rotation-invariant systems. The driven dynamics map onto mutually orthogonal Krylov subspaces, and the spread complexity depends only on the spectral properties of the initial Hamiltonian and the driving schedule. The method extends to Liouville space to treat the Krylov dynamics of initial thermal states. The authors also discuss observables in scale-invariant quantum gases and rotation-invariant spin systems.

entry.title: Trapping neutral atoms with light's magnetic field via magnetic-dipole transitions
entry.summary: Optical trapping of neutral atoms via magnetic-dipole transitions arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper shows that the magnetic field of light acting on a magnetic-dipole (M1) transition can produce an ac Zeeman shift larger than the ac Stark shift, enabling magnetic trapping of neutral atoms. Optical trapping of such atoms is usually described as an electric-dipole effect. The authors construct the M1 polarizability tensor and identify a critical detuning below which the magnetic interaction dominates. They analyze trapping parameters and loss mechanisms for erbium and dysprosium transitions and propose two trapping configurations.

entry.title: Controlled state preparation and guaranteed transport on a fluctuating quantum graph
entry.summary: Controlled preparation and unconditional transport on a fluctuating quantum graph arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies whether a prescribed input can be prepared and transmitted with appreciable probability on a quantum graph with fluctuating edges. The authors use a one-probe model on a square candidate lattice, combining a generalized Rokhsar–Kivelson parent, spectral reduction, adiabatic preparation, and local dynamical estimates. Assuming a supplied coherent graph ground state, they prove an arrival probability of at least 5/8 in a specified receiver region of a sufficiently large finite open square, and at least 9/16 under explicit local error bounds.

entry.title: A new framework for quantum reinforcement learning, treating agent, environment, and rewards as quantum
entry.summary: A New Framework for Quantum Reinforcement Learning arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper notes that most quantum reinforcement learning still uses a classical interface that relies on measurements, which can discard entanglement. The authors introduce a fully quantum framework in which both the policy and the environment are modeled as conditional quantum channels. They propose a quantum policy-gradient algorithm with a trainable control basis and a new parameter-shift rule for finite- and infinite-horizon gradient estimation. They also show that the resulting stochastic gradient ascent converges to stationary points under standard assumptions.

entry.title: Shot- and noise-aware Pauli correlation encoding for Max-Cut experiments on IBM Heron
entry.summary: Shot- and Noise-Aware Pauli Correlation Encoding for Max-Cut Experiments on IBM Heron Quantum Processor arXiv · Oct 14, 2026The paper studies Pauli correlation encoding (PCE) for the Max-Cut problem and shows that the sharpness parameter in its training loss acts as a hidden shot budget. The authors propose a schedule that sets sharpness according to the number of measurement shots, which outperforms published schedules on five G-set graphs in simulation. On the IBM Heron processor ibm_fez, a 96-CZ hardware-native circuit retained up to 0.919 of the best-known cut. Correction Nov 13, 2026: Marked withdrawn by its source; no longer a pick

entry.title: Dynamical Casimir emission from Floquet-driven Landau polaritons; gauge invariance rules out a superradiant transition
entry.summary: Dynamical Casimir emission from Floquet-driven Landau polaritons: Gauge invariance forbids a superradiant phase transition arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies Landau polaritons formed by a two-dimensional electron gas in a terahertz cavity under periodic driving. The authors argue that gauge invariance forbids a superradiant phase transition even with magnetic modulation. Instead, magnetic modulation produces dynamical Casimir emission, including Faraday-driven polariton–magnetoplasmon pairs and two-color photon pairs with up to 5–10 dB of two-mode squeezing. ★★★★ Notable: The authors attribute the predicted Floquet SRPT to improper averaging, give a gauge-invariance argument, and predict dynamical Casimir two-color photon pairs with up to 5–10 dB squeezing.

entry.title: Maximal Violation of Mermin Inequality for Commuting von Neumann Algebras and Multipartite Vacuum Entanglement in QFT
entry.summary: Maximal Violation of Mermin Inequality for Commuting von Neumann Algebras and Multipartite Vacuum Entanglement in QFT arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies how strongly the Mermin inequality, a multipartite Bell-type test, can be violated by three or more mutually commuting von Neumann algebras. It extends earlier two-party results by Summers and Werner for relativistic quantum field theory vacua. For the tripartite Mermin functional, maximal violation in every normal state is shown to be equivalent to the existence of a common sequence of asymptotic GHZ stabilizers. Strong stability of each local factor is necessary, and embedding an infinite GHZ tensor product is sufficient. Counterexamples show that strong stability, type III_1 and tripartite duality alone are insufficient. The results extend to n≥3 parties. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend Summers-Werner's two-party Bell result to multipartite Mermin inequalities, giving an equivalence criterion and counterexamples.

entry.title: Matroid entropy, matrix concentration, and sharp inequalities
entry.summary: Lorentzian entropy, subgaussian matrix concentration, and sharp functional inequalities for all matroids arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper proves complete entropy contraction for homogeneous Lorentzian laws and derives subgaussian matrix concentration and sharp functional inequalities for every matroid. It shows that retaining ℓ of r particles contracts matrix entropy by the optimal universal factor ℓ/r, and gives Chernoff and Bernstein bounds for basis sums. For unit-edge matroid basis graphs it establishes cube-type small-set and Gross inequalities, classifies their equality cases, and characterizes extremal eigenfunctions and entropy extremizers. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors extend homogeneous Lorentzian entropy contraction to all matroids, report subgaussian matrix concentration and functional inequalities, state an optimal complete entropy-decay rate of four

entry.title: Nonperturbative string dynamics on a superconducting quantum processor: a quantum simulation study of how electric flux strings in a 2D gauge theory evolve through charge motion, pair creation and transverse deformation.
entry.summary: Nonperturbative string dynamics in a (2+1)D lattice gauge theory on a superconducting quantum processor arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper uses 63 superconducting qubits, including 12 ancillas, to simulate a (2+1)D Z2 lattice gauge theory with dynamical matter and an explicit magnetic plaquette interaction. It covers both strongly confined and nonperturbative deconfined regimes. In the deconfined regime, charge and flux spread rapidly, matter occupation in the string interior increases near the pair-creation resonance, and spreading is suppressed at strong electric fields. Local Gauss-law constraints are used for error detection, together with ancilla checks and noise rescaling, to measure dynamics in circuits with up to 15 second-order Trotter steps. ★★★★ Notable: The authors simulate nonperturbative (2+1)D Z2 string dynamics on 63 superconducting qubits, using Gauss-law constraints for error detection.

entry.title: Error Resilience and Unitary 2-Designs: a paper on how quantum information is protected from errors in encoding-error-decoding circuits, and how departures from unitary 2-design encoders affect that protection.
entry.summary: Error Resilience and Unitary 2-Designs arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies how quantum information is protected in encoding-error-decoding circuits, where recovery fidelity approaches unity below a threshold error strength. The authors show that departures from Haar second-moment statistics of the encoder can destabilize this error-protecting phase. They derive a universal inequality linking recovery fidelity to the second unitary frame potential. Matchgate circuits with tunable non-Gaussian gates and Hamiltonian encoders serve as examples, and recovery fidelity is proposed as a diagnostic of unitary 2-design behavior. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive a universal inequality linking recovery fidelity to unitary frame potential, illustrated with doped matchgate circuits and Hamiltonian encoders.

entry.title: Reading long-range information from separable quantum records needs entangled measurements
entry.summary: Reading long-range information from a separable quantum record requires entangled measurements arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper studies qubit probes that record the relative orientation of neighboring Ising spins, yielding a fully separable probe record. On the square lattice, readout with separable measurements has success probability approaching 1/2 as spin separation grows, for 0<p≤1-1/√2. A joint readout of the same record keeps success probability above 1/2 by a distance-independent margin for p between 0.29181 and 1. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show long-range information in a separable quantum record requires entangled measurements, with a strict overlap interval separating two readout strategies on the square lattice.

entry.title: CV-TF-QKD: continuous-variable twin-field quantum key distribution
entry.summary: CV-TF-QKD arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper introduces a continuous-variable version of twin-field quantum key distribution using independent Gaussian-modulated coherent states and an untrusted single-photon relay. Two protocols, full-record reconciliation and binary phase disclosure, achieve nearly equal asymptotic key rates against collective attacks. The authors also establish composable security against general coherent attacks and report finite-key calculations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend twin-field QKD to Gaussian-modulated coherent states, reporting composable security proofs and finite-key rates above repeaterless bounds.

entry.title: Sample cost of learning Gaussian quantum states with single-copy and entangled measurements
entry.summary: Sample complexity of learning fermionic and bosonic Gaussian states with single-copy and entangled measurements arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies how many copies of a quantum state are needed to learn it to a given trace-distance accuracy. Under single-copy measurements, it shows that learning mixed fermionic Gaussian states on m modes requires Θ(m³/ε²) copies, resolving Conjecture 10.1 of arXiv:2609.23189. It also gives corresponding sample-complexity results for block measurements on k copies and for bosonic Gaussian states. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report an upper bound of m^3/ε² single-copy samples for mixed fermionic Gaussian state learning, resolving a conjecture and filling a sample-complexity table across measurement types.

entry.title: Key Readiness and Authentication-Key Replenishment for Quantum-Secured UAV Edge Computing
entry.summary: Finite-Key Readiness and Authentication-Key Replenishment in QKD-Assisted UAV Edge Computing arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies the time and energy cost of obtaining fresh quantum keys from a finite-key decoy-state BB84 protocol for a UAV serving ground gateways in edge computing. It uses a count-level Monte Carlo model reproduced by a semi-analytic model to link key acceptance to protected upload, computation, and download. At 26 dB optical loss, fresh keys raise the 95th-percentile completion time of both tasks from 10.37 s to 28.65 s, and hover energy grows accordingly.

entry.title: Correlation structure in the single-j nuclear model via quantum information theory
entry.summary: Structure of correlations for the single-j model using quantum information theory arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies correlations in the mean-field ground state of the single-j model, a realistic fermionic nuclear model with abelian and non-abelian broken symmetries. The authors find that the two types of symmetry breaking affect correlations within the mean-field state very differently, which casts doubt on symmetry breaking as a mechanism for absorbing maximum correlations. They also report that symmetry restoration redistributes existing fake correlations between paired orbitals into more complex subsystems.

entry.title: A quantum thermal transistor based on nonlinear coupling to the environment
entry.summary: Quantum Thermal Transistor via Nonlinear Environmental Coupling arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies a harmonic oscillator coupled to emitter, collector, and base thermal reservoirs, showing that thermal amplification is absent when only single-quantum exchange occurs. Introducing weak nonlinearity that permits two-quantum exchange at the emitter enables amplification. The authors also propose a realization using a longitudinally coupled auxiliary two-level system with bath spectral filtering.

entry.title: Multidimensional Quantum Block Turbo Codes: extending quantum turbo decoding to multi-layer product codes
entry.summary: Multidimensional Quantum Block Turbo Codes arXiv · Nov 11, 2026Quantum serial turbo codes and quantum block turbo codes brought iterative turbo decoding into quantum error-correcting codes. This paper presents a theory of multidimensional quantum block turbo codes, a turbo decoding method for multi-layer product codes. The authors describe the algorithm and simulate the performance of the three-dimensional case on a depolarizing channel.

entry.title: Simulating light-matter lattice dynamics on fault-tolerant quantum computers
entry.summary: Simulating closed- and open-system dynamics of Tavis--Cummings lattices on fault-tolerant quantum computers arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper analyzes the logical resources needed to simulate real-time dynamics of a two-dimensional Tavis–Cummings lattice, where cavities hold several emitters coupled to photons. The authors build circuits for photon hopping and local light–matter exchange that update photon occupations in place, removing an auxiliary photon register. Across three examples, the controlled walk uses 4.75% to 8.11% fewer Toffoli gates than a two-register implementation. Closed-system evolution uses generalized quantum signal processing, while open systems use a sampled first-order dilation.

entry.title: On-chip dissipation for fast superconducting qubit reset
entry.summary: Implementing rapid reset of superconducting qubits with on-chip dissipation arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper experimentally demonstrates a scalable method for resetting superconducting transmon qubits and removing leakage, using dedicated dissipation units made of resonators coupled to on-chip resistive loads. The design provides Purcell protection while isolating the qubits from warmer external circuitry. The reported median reset time constant for the |g⟩-|e⟩ transition is about 48 ns, at an effective bath temperature of 30 mK.

entry.title: How Invariance Helps Quantum Neural Networks Avoid Overfitting and Shortcut Learning
entry.summary: Invariance can prevent overfitting and shortcut learning in Quantum Neural Networks arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies the effect of building rotation and reflection invariance (dihedral group D4) into quantum neural networks, comparing eight-qubit models with identical encoding, circuit structure and parameter counts. On four binary tasks, including MNIST and galaxy and red blood cell datasets, invariant models trained on a few tens of images generalized better than non-invariant ones. When trained with a class-dependent corner watermark, non-invariant models learned the watermark and often fell to chance level once it was moved, while invariant models were unaffected. The accuracy advantage of invariant models also persists under a realistic noise model.

entry.title: Fast control of fluxonium qubits using picosecond pulses from Josephson digital circuits
entry.summary: High-Speed Control of a Fluxonium Qubit via Picosecond Pulses from Josephson Digital Circuits arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper presents a method for controlling fluxonium qubits with picosecond single-flux-quantum (SFQ) pulses generated by Josephson digital circuits. Because SFQ protocols designed for transmons perform poorly on low-frequency fluxonium, the authors propose two complementary approaches: one applies high-frequency SFQ pulse packets through the flux channel, and the other combines phase-shifted flux and charge pulses to shorten gate duration. Multilevel simulations show single-qubit gate fidelities above 99.99%.

entry.title: A new computational model for spin-free sum-of-squares energy bounds of electronic Hamiltonians
entry.summary: A New Computational Model for the Spin-Free Sum-of-Squares Energy Bounds of Electronic Hamiltonian arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper reformulates the spin-free sum-of-squares (SOS) energy bound optimization for electronic Hamiltonians, which normally yields large semidefinite programs, as a convex quadratic problem over one symmetric matrix. It gives explicit maps between solutions of the two formulations and identifies the Frank–Wolfe gap with the difference between primal and dual objectives. GPU-accelerated Coulomb contractions and a cached fully corrective Frank–Wolfe method are used to solve it, with tests on 65 FCIDUMP models and hydrogen rings up to 10,000 orbitals.

entry.title: Electrical Stark Tuning and In Situ Field Sensing of V2 Silicon Vacancies in a-Plane 4H-SiC Lateral pin-Diodes
entry.summary: Electrical Stark Tuning and In Situ Field Sensing of V₂ Silicon Vacancies in a 4H-SiC a-Plane Lateral pin-Diode arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The study fabricates lateral pin-diodes on a-plane 4H-SiC wafers using a scalable CMOS process and demonstrates electrical control and optical addressing of V2 silicon vacancy color centers in their intrinsic region. The embedded centers measure local electric fields at cryogenic temperatures via the Stark effect, and the results are compared with TCAD simulations. Reverse-bias Stark tuning is also used to align the zero-phonon lines of individual emitters, which remain spectrally stable for over four hours.

entry.title: Edge quantum weight of finite Chern flakes and the lower bound it imposes
entry.summary: Edge quantum weight of finite Chern flakes and its topological floor arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper studies how the edge of a finite Chern insulator flake contributes to the quantum weight that governs a circuit's zero-point energy. It shows that the dipole weight of low-frequency edge transitions is at least |C| per unit area. The measured weight depends on whether the circuit is slower or faster than the edge modes. Exact free-fermion calculations on lattice flakes support this bound and its dependence on circuit frequency.

entry.title: A classical post-processing method that recovers aliased energies in unitary quantum Krylov diagonalization
entry.summary: Classical phase unwrapping enables large-time-step unitary quantum Krylov subspace diagonalization arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper addresses molecular energy calculations on early fault-tolerant quantum hardware using unitary quantum Krylov subspace diagonalization (UQKSD). It notes that small time steps produce ill-conditioned overlap matrices, while larger steps improve conditioning but leave energies known only modulo 2π/τ. The authors propose CURE-QKSD, a classical post-processing method that recovers the missing multiples of 2π/τ from phase-consistency landscapes of one or two UQKSD runs, leaving the circuits unchanged. In noiseless tests on six molecules with 12 to 20 qubits, all 28 targeted energies were recovered, and under Gaussian noise, aliased time steps reached chemical accuracy with smaller Krylov bases.

entry.title: Disorder-driven logarithmic spreading and localization of quantum fluctuations
entry.summary: Disorder-Induced Logarithmic Spreading and Localization of Quantum Fluctuations arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper studies how quantum fluctuations beyond mean-field dynamics propagate in weakly interacting disordered bosonic systems, comparing the Bose-Hubbard model with the Gross-Pitaevskii equation. In contrast to ballistic spreading without disorder, the fluctuations spread logarithmically at intermediate times under random and quasiperiodic disorder before saturating. The spreading rate decreases algebraically with disorder strength, and this behavior persists across particle numbers and in two dimensions.

entry.title: Truncating low-energy spectral windows in compact U(1) lattice gauge theory
entry.summary: Low-energy spectral-window truncation for compact U(1) lattice gauge theory arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper proves a non-asymptotic bound on the error from truncating electric flux in the low-energy window of the pure compact U(1) lattice Hamiltonian. The bound holds for all normalized vectors in that window on a three-dimensional periodic cubic lattice at zero theta, in the gauge-invariant zero-global-flux sector. An analytic finite-volume strong-coupling example illustrates a preserved non-vacuum band and plaquette signal. The estimate also yields precision-dependent sufficient cutoffs and local electric-square readout bounds.

entry.title: Quantum-informed graph decomposition: shrinking graphs with QAOA to solve MaxCut more accurately
entry.summary: Quantum-Informed Graph Decomposition arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper proposes Quantum Enhanced Graph Decomposition (QEGD), a heuristic that uses QAOA as a subroutine to sparsify graphs through local vertex merging. Applied to MaxCut problems solved with QAOA, it achieves higher approximation ratios than GDOA on all tested random 5-regular and 6-regular graphs. On Erdős-Rényi graphs, it reports higher average approximation ratios than QAOA² and ParaQAOA, and compared with DC-QAOA it is higher on sparse graphs and comparable on denser ones. Its average wall-clock time is between 0.4% and 5% of DC-QAOA's.

entry.title: Quantum-enhanced QSAR for DYRK1A: comparing two molecular representations
entry.summary: Quantum-Enhanced QSAR for DYRK1A: Evaluating Complementary and Utility QPU-Derived Molecular Representations arXiv · Nov 11, 2026The paper applies the same RBF-SVM to DYRK1A kinase compounds using either tabular molecular descriptors or a vector measured on a quantum processor. The two models propose different sets of compounds for experimental evaluation, and each includes some already-labeled actives that the other omits. The authors report these differences without claiming formal quantum advantage or explaining why the two vectors separate differently.

entry.title: Quantum Advantage in Assisted Work Distillation via Complementary Correlations
entry.summary: Quantum Advantage in Assisted Work Distillation from Complementary Correlations arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper links microscale work extraction in thermal operations with the characterization of nonclassical correlations in bipartite quantum systems. It treats correlations measured across mutually unbiased bases as an energy resource for local work extraction and derives work-based steering inequalities whose violations certify a one-sided device-independent thermodynamic enhancement. Under a one-sided semi-device-independent framework with restricted untrusted dimension, it introduces dynamically scaling work inequalities that witness superunsteerability in weakly correlated entangled states.

entry.title: Multiparticle entanglement in a time-dependent electron–ion–photon system
entry.summary: Multiparticle entanglement in a time-dependent electron--ion--photon system arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies how entanglement evolves over time in a composite system of an electron, an ion, and a photon produced by photoionization. The authors measure entanglement using the von Neumann entropy of one-versus-rest bipartitions, showing that the initial electron–ion entangled state passes through a genuinely multiparticle-entangled state before approaching an electron–photon entangled state. Logarithmic negativity reveals pairwise entanglement, including transient ion–photon entanglement, and high-dimensional entanglement linked to the photon-energy continuum.

entry.title: Theory paper on how coherent and dissipative mechanisms interact to synchronize quantum oscillators
entry.summary: Coherent-Dissipative Crossover of Quantum Synchronization arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies synchronization between two quantum oscillators coupled through a fast mediator. Using adiabatic elimination, the authors identify two channels, coherent exchange and collective dissipation, and give an analytical description linking dissipation-dominated and coherence-dominated regimes. They find synchronization depends on the joint balance of coherent coupling, dissipation, and reservoir-induced fluctuations. Continuous monitoring of the shared output enhances conditional synchronization, with the largest gain near the coherent-dissipative crossover.

entry.title: Cross-platform benchmark of GHZ-state generation on cloud-accessed quantum processors
entry.summary: Cross-Platform Benchmarking of GHZ-State Generation in Quantum Processors via Cloud Services arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper benchmarks nine commercially available superconducting and trapped-ion quantum processors from five vendors, accessed through cloud services. Using the multipartite entanglement benchmark from the QuSquare suite, it estimates the fidelity of GHZ states without error mitigation. The largest GHZ state passing the benchmark is far smaller than the total qubit count of each processor, with the best superconducting devices reaching 27 and 24 qubits and the 12-qubit trapped-ion processor passing with its full register. The authors also find that median calibration data poorly predict outcomes and that the statistical decision rule strongly affects results.

entry.title: Study showing initial-state memory in long-time dynamics is revealed through non-Gaussianity
entry.summary: Memory of Initial States in Long-Time Dynamics Revealed by Non-Gaussianity arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies quantum dynamics of few-body observables in quadratic systems. The authors generate a family of non-Gaussian initial states and quantify their non-Gaussianity using the corresponding entropy. They find that the size of temporal fluctuations is a smooth function of this non-Gaussianity, which explains why fluctuations after quantum quenches scale exponentially small for non-Gaussian states and polynomially small for Gaussian states.

entry.title: Two atoms interacting strongly through light-induced dipoles
entry.summary: Two atoms with strong light-induced dipolar interactions arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies how two atoms scatter light when placed closer than one optical wavelength, revealing new effects from strong interactions between laser-induced electric dipoles. It reports a narrow density range where part of the scattered light is coherent, with a collective enhancement factor of two relative to independent atoms. The authors also show that the probe laser intensity can modify the scattering length, offering a new way to shift Feshbach resonances.

entry.title: Dynamical GKP codes: quantum error correction combining oscillator lattice encodings with time-dependent measurements
entry.summary: Dynamical GKP codes arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper extends dynamical quantum codes, which protect information with sequences of measurements, to Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes that encode qubits in oscillators' continuous phase space. The authors build subsystem GKP codes from scaled symplectic lattices and give a method to compute a dynamical GKP code's syndrome and distance from a persistent stabilizer lattice and a bounded inference window. They illustrate the framework with a two-mode square-hexagonal Floquet GKP code, which has lower measurement weight than the square and hexagonal GKP codes while combining their logical gates.

entry.title: PINNverse Meets Jordan-Wigner: Learning Spin-Chain Hamiltonians
entry.summary: PINNverse meets Jordan--Wigner: learning the Hamiltonian of long spin chains arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper uses physics-informed neural networks (PINNverse) to infer the parameters of a quantum Hamiltonian from measured expectation values. With the Jordan-Wigner transformation, the dynamics closes on an N×N one-body density matrix, so the network needs only N² outputs and local observables measured in five global settings. On synthetic data, the method recovers parameters for spin chains of up to 50 qubits, with couplings learned to better than 0.1%. Errors in local frequencies of long chains are corrected by a least-squares fit initialized from the network estimate.

entry.title: Pool-free, residual-triggered circuit growth for variational imaginary-time evolution
entry.summary: Pool-free, residual-triggered ansatz growth for variational imaginary-time evolution: when a fixed operator order beats adaptive screening arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies a method for growing quantum circuits in variational imaginary-time evolution (VITE). Layers are fixed in advance from nested commutators of the Hamiltonian, and a new layer is added only when the relative McLachlan residual exceeds a threshold, so no operator pool is needed. On five non-integrable systems, the method reaches a relative error of 10^-4 with 1.6 to 5.4 times fewer circuits than the cheapest of six to eight adaptive variants. The advantage disappears on transverse-field Ising models and is not evident at a tighter target of 10^-6.

entry.title: Quantum propagation of vibrational excitation in a trapped-ion crystal: experiments on how localized phonons move along a chain of ions
entry.summary: Quantum propagation of vibrational excitation in harmonically confined trapped-ion crystal arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper experimentally studies how a localized vibrational excitation, or local phonon, propagates through a one-dimensional trapped-ion crystal. The experiment uses a 10-ion crystal confined in a harmonic potential. The authors find that unevenness in ion spacing produces behaviors such as adjacent hopping and global movement, and the results agree with numerical simulations in fine detail.

entry.title: Estimating coupling strengths in circulant networks with multiparameter quantum methods
entry.summary: Multiparameter quantum estimation of circulant networks arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies how continuous-time quantum walks can be used to estimate coupling strengths in circulant networks. The authors derive the quantum Fisher information matrix, identify optimal probe states, and determine the ultimate precision quantum measurements allow, including how it scales with the number of unknown couplings. They also compare position measurements with the quantum limit and find that coarse-grained, lower-resolution measurements can sometimes outperform finer ones.

entry.title: Reservoir-driven quantum phase transitions in spin ensembles: an open-system study
entry.summary: Reservoir-induced Quantum Phase Transitions in spin ensembles arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies an open quantum system of many two-level atoms coupled to bosonic reservoirs. The authors show that, without a counterterm and lacking a metastable minimum, the system can undergo a quantum phase transition set by the reservoir structure rather than by internal coherent dynamics. Using exact quantum Langevin equations, they locate the critical point from the complex excitation spectrum and derive reflection and transmission spectra showing mode softening and increasingly asymmetric lineshapes near the transition.

entry.title: Correlations carried and controlled by coupled non-Markovian environments
entry.summary: Correlations carried and controlled by coupled non-Markovian environments arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper presents a local hierarchy of pure states for quantum systems coupled to spatially correlated, non-Markovian environments with memory. Using a chain of locally coupled Rabi spin-cavity pairs, it shows how photon hopping between cavities creates correlations and entanglement between otherwise isolated spins. It also examines how monitoring intermediate cavities and feeding measurement results back to spins affects correlations between endpoint spins.

entry.title: Lattice Hamiltonians for Chiral Gauge Theories
entry.summary: Lattice Hamiltonians for Chiral Gauge Theories arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper presents a lattice Hamiltonian for chiral gauge theories on the boundary of a slab. The formulation is gauge-fixed, so gauge variables are the physical modes of the boundary field, and Gauss's law holds exactly. The bulk gauge field is determined by the boundary field and an integer label, the topological charge that the boundary generates and the bulk stores as a localized instanton. After Pauli-Villars subtraction, sectors differing by a unit of bulk charge are shown to be degenerate, the mirror fermions decouple, and the boundary theory has no vacuum angle.

entry.title: Testing how well a gauge-invariant tensor network state captures a topological phase transition
entry.summary: Assessing the expressive power of a gauge-invariant PEPS ansatz across a topological phase transition arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies the GGFPEPS ansatz, a gauge-invariant tensor network state for (2+1)-dimensional lattice gauge theories. The authors recast the calculation as a Grassmann tensor network contracted deterministically with HOTRG and CTMRG, reaching lattice sizes up to L=34. They report that an ansatz with only eight complex variational parameters describes the pure Z2 gauge theory accurately, including the topological phase transition region.

entry.title: Fast coherent readout of neutral-atom qubits using homodyne detection of resonant fluorescence
entry.summary: Coherent Optical Readout of Neutral-Atom Qubits via Homodyne Detection of Resonant Fluorescence arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper proposes reading out the state of neutral-atom qubits by balanced homodyne detection of their resonant fluorescence with photodiodes, avoiding the electronic latency of camera-based detection. An analytic model describes how atomic motion affects the time-integrated quadrature signal and noise, identifying an optimal detection time. Three-dimensional Monte Carlo simulations validate the model.

entry.title: Analog quantum optimization for weighted MaxCut on a 3D Rydberg atom array
entry.summary: Analog quantum approximate optimization algorithm for solving the weighted MaxCut problem on three-dimensional single-atom Rydberg array arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper theoretically studies an analog version of the quantum approximate optimization algorithm for the weighted maximum cut problem. It uses a three-dimensional array of trapped Rydberg atoms driven by global laser pulses, with weights encoded in interatomic interactions. The authors compare discretized quantum annealing with a graph neural network warm-start strategy on twenty random 12-vertex 3-regular graphs. Noiseless results are compared against Goemans-Williamson rounding.

entry.title: Imaging the modes and fields of a compact superconducting resonator array
entry.summary: Eigenmode and field imaging of a compact superconducting resonator array arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies a two-dimensional honeycomb array of 33 lumped-element superconducting resonators that hosts topological edge states. The authors combine laser scanning microscopy (LSM), which images the eigenmodes, with nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center magnetometry, which maps the local microwave magnetic field amplitude. Using this spatial information, they confirm that the fabricated lattice matches the design, image the topological edge state and measure its sublattice polarization, and bound the relative on-site frequency disorder to about 0.3%.

entry.title: Quantum-assisted anomaly detection study comparing latent prior distributions
entry.summary: Quantum-Assisted Generative Anomaly Detection: A Dimension-Controlled Study of Latent Refinement arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper examines how the choice of latent prior distribution affects anomaly-based malware detection. Building on SAGEGAN, which is trained only on benign data, the authors compare a 512-dimensional Gaussian, a 48-dimensional Gaussian, and a 48-dimensional distribution sampled from a photonic quantum processor. They refine each frozen model representation using greedy and reinforcement-learning methods. The quantum-derived model shows richer latent structure and benefits most from refinement, while final detection accuracy is similar to the refined Gaussian latent model.

entry.title: Observation of strong electric dipole-dipole interactions between two atoms, a measurement of how paired atoms couple through their electric dipoles
entry.summary: Observation of strong electric dipole-dipole interactions between two atoms arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The authors prepared pairs of atoms at densities above 10^16 per cubic centimeter and studied how they interact with light. In this regime the coherent part of the electric dipole-dipole interaction exceeds the dissipative part. Off-resonant laser light dresses the atoms with a dipole moment of about 1 Debye, and the resonance of two atoms shifts through a two-body Lamb shift dominated by the near-field dipolar interaction.

entry.title: A quantum algorithm for efficiently preparing equal superpositions over any integer range
entry.summary: An Efficient Quantum Algorithm for Preparing Uniform Superpositions over Arbitrary Integer Intervals arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper presents a method for exactly preparing a uniform quantum state over any nonempty range of integer labels in an n-qubit register. The circuit uses no ancilla qubits and only single-qubit and singly controlled single-qubit gates.
