The direct construction has a worst-case gate count of 5n-9 for n≥3, and a worst-case lower bound of Ω(n) shows asymptotic optimality in register width.

entry.title: Routing quantum-classical hybrid packets across multiple hops, one packet at a time.
entry.summary: Packet-wise multi-hop quantum routing of hybrid quantum-classical packets arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper presents a fiber-based quantum router that forwards hybrid packets, combining classical headers and quantum payloads, with less disturbance and latency by avoiding header regeneration. The authors experimentally demonstrate double-hop routing through two cascaded routers to three different receivers. Quantum key distribution packets using time-bin qubits and the BB84 protocol with a two-decoy-state method were delivered to all three receivers, achieving nonzero secret key rates.

entry.title: Fully GPU-accelerated semistochastic Epstein-Nesbet perturbation theory
entry.summary: Fully GPU-accelerated semistochastic Epstein-Nesbet perturbation theory arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper presents a fully GPU-accelerated, distributed implementation of semistochastic second-order Epstein-Nesbet perturbation theory (EN-PT2) for improving selected configuration interaction energies. It fuses excitation generation, screening, and PT2 weighting into one kernel traversal and uses fixed-size random-phase CountSketch arrays to limit memory and replace large external determinant exchange. On one A100 GPU it runs 8.21 to 37.53 times faster than Arrow on 64 CPU cores at the same statistical standard error, and it reaches 93.5% parallel efficiency on 16 GPUs across two nodes.

entry.title: Quantum-walk proton transport oracle and amplitude estimation of range statistics in therapy
entry.summary: Quantum-walk transport oracles and amplitude estimation of a scalar range statistic in proton therapy arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper proposes a discrete-time quantum-walk oracle for proton transport, in which an energy register is driven by an energy-dependent coin encoding a continuous-slowing-down stopping-power surrogate, so stochastic energy loss and range straggling emerge from circuit dynamics. On this oracle, the probability that a proton penetrates beyond a distal depth threshold is formulated as a marked amplitude and estimated with maximum-likelihood amplitude estimation. The reported Bragg-shaped depth-deposit profile agrees with a classical Monte Carlo of identical rules to within 0.27%. A resource analysis finds the logical gate cost per oracle call exceeds the permitted budget by 160 to 5400 times at clinical scale.

entry.title: Real-time spectral combs from delayed quantum feedback in multimode cavity QED
entry.summary: Real-time spectral combs from delayed quantum feedback in multimode cavity QED arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies the time-dependent physical spectrum of light from a two-level atom coupled to many discrete modes of an electromagnetic cavity. Radiation emitted by the atom returns after a round-trip time and re-excites it, producing repeated population revivals. Using an analytical solution, the authors show that during these revivals a transient frequency comb with spacing 2π/t_r develops.

entry.title: Enhanced control and magnetic sensing of spin defects in boron nitride using two quantum transitions at once
entry.summary: Double-quantum enhanced coherent control and magnetic sensing of spin defects in hexagonal boron nitride arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies the negatively charged boron vacancy spin defect in hexagonal boron nitride, driving two ground-state transitions simultaneously to coherently control the Δm_s=2 manifold. Compared with the single-quantum method under identical conditions, the double-quantum approach improves optical readout contrast and gives a 2.6-fold signal-to-noise gain in AC magnetometry. The authors also use the double-quantum relaxation channel as a differential probe of electric-field and strain noise and assess which noise models are consistent with the data.

entry.title: PriorTilt: decoding quantum error-correcting codes by sparsely adjusting belief propagation priors
entry.summary: PriorTilt: Decoding quantum LDPC codes with sparse perturbations of belief propagation priors arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper introduces PriorTilt, a variant of belief propagation (BP) decoding that shifts a small fraction of prior log-likelihood ratios using offsets based on posterior and outgoing-message statistics, keeping the message-passing rules unchanged. In circuit-level decoding of three benchmark codes, PriorTilt achieves lower logical error rates than Relay-BP and a beam search decoder. For the [[144,12,12]] Gross code BB144 at noise rate 10^-3, the logical error rate reductions reach 4.3 times relative to Relay-BP and 3.1 times relative to the beam search decoder.

entry.title: Syndrome extraction for quantum LDPC codes in silicon using distributed entanglement and mobile ancillas
entry.summary: Syndrome extraction for quantum LDPC codes in silicon: Distributed entanglement and mobile ancillas arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper develops a spin-singlet architecture on a silicon node network for bivariate-bicycle quantum error-correcting codes. Singlets are generated on shuttling lanes, distributed between nodes, and consumed to measure non-local stabilizers. Two syndrome-extraction circuits, based on distributed GHZ states and ancilla teleportation, are compared against the CAbLECAR scheme. The results show that physical layout and interaction order matter as much as the choice of circuit, and that cleaner entangled resources do not necessarily yield a more reliable logical memory.

entry.title: The energy cost of loading classical data into quantum computers
entry.summary: The energetic cost of loading classical data in quantum computers arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper treats loading classical data into a quantum random access memory (QRAM) as a physical hardware process and quantifies the dynamic energy used by one query on a superconducting processor. It accounts for attenuation across a multi-stage refrigerator, thermal photons, and gate errors, and analyzes a linear-depth multiplexer and a bucket-brigade architecture. For a representative query with a 12-qubit address register, the authors report a fidelity of 0.969, 3.51×10⁻⁴ J of dynamic energy, and average and peak power of 4.38 W and 64.4 W. They also find that at fixed target fidelity, the operating point and attenuation profile can change average power by a factor of two or more.

entry.title: Operational limits of reference renewal for retained quantum-service results
entry.summary: Operational limits of reference renewal for retained quantum-service results arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper applies reference renewal to re-examine retained physical quantum-service results under a prespecified protocol. Of twelve transitions, ten completed renewal and eight met the prespecified endpoint, with five succeeding using retained results alone. The authors report that incomplete references, binding failures and sequential waits reveal operational limits, and that the exact one-sided test does not establish the recovery hypothesis.

entry.title: Quantum-assisted regret minimization for solving bounded-payoff imperfect-information games more efficiently
entry.summary: Quantum-Assisted Counterfactual Regret Minimization for Bounded-Payoff Imperfect-Information Games arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper proposes Quantum-Assisted Counterfactual Regret Minimization, a framework for computing equilibria in bounded-payoff imperfect-information games. It uses Quantum Amplitude Estimation to reduce the computational complexity of regret updates while preserving the convergence of the classical method. The authors analyze the resulting exploitability bound and discuss NISQ-compatible amplitude-estimation variants and their resource requirements.

entry.title: Neural flow models that simulate quantum circuits classically in phase space
entry.summary: Normalizing Flows for Classical Simulation of Quantum Circuits in Phase Space arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper presents a framework that learns representations of quantum circuits using the phase space formulation of many-body systems. It treats N-qubit states as probability distributions on a smooth 2N-dimensional manifold and parameterizes unitary gates as normalizing flows between these distributions. The authors evaluate the method on three common families of quantum circuits. They report that its accuracy exceeds that of current state-of-the-art neural network methods for large system sizes.

entry.title: Adaptive Policy-Guided Error Mitigation (APGEM): A Learning Framework for Noise-Resilient Quantum Machine Learning
entry.summary: Adaptive Policy-Guided Error Mitigation (APGEM): A Unified Learning-Based Framework for Noise Resilience in Quantum Machine Learning arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper introduces APGEM, a framework that uses a contextual-bandit controller to choose among error mitigation techniques at each step, based on feedback signals the algorithm already produces. The choices include zero-noise extrapolation, probabilistic error cancellation, measurement error mitigation, dynamical decoupling, and circuit optimization. The framework applies across supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement, and hybrid learning. Across 80 algorithm-and-noise conditions, adaptive selection reached 95.5% of an oracle that always picks the best technique and outperformed six fixed strategies. On noise models from eight real IBM devices, it achieved 99.9% of oracle utility.

entry.title: Polynomial quantum recurrent channels for matrix inversion: reset dynamics and Chebyshev filtering
entry.summary: Polynomial Quantum Recurrent Channels for Matrix Inverse Actions: Deferred-Reset Dynamics and Chebyshev Filtering arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper develops completely positive, trace-preserving polynomial recurrent quantum channels for preparing quantum solution states and derives fixed-point and time-varying tracking error bounds. In 2,880 synthetic configurations, resident Chebyshev recurrence increased the number of snapshots passing the accuracy criterion in 608 cases, tied in 2,271, and lost in one. A cost study over 360 scenarios found fresh recurrence cheaper in all 184 jointly feasible cases, while resident recurrence alone met the accuracy requirements in 74 cases. At a logical noise rate of 10^-4, neither recurrent method qualified. The results show conditional tracking advantages but no general end-to-end speedup or total-cost benefit.

entry.title: Hardware-trained quantum circuit generator for diagonalizing organotin hydroxides on up to 70 qubits
entry.summary: A Hardware-Trained Generative Quantum Eigensolver for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization of Organotin Hydroxides up to 70 Qubits arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper trains generative quantum eigensolver policies on the IBM Heron processor ibm_kobe to produce state-preparation circuits for sample-based quantum diagonalization. Training starts on a noiseless simulator and then runs at 46 and 70 qubits with hardware in the loop. Policies trained on transition-metal complexes are applied without retraining to organotin photoresist models from 32 to 70 qubits. Most runs land within 15 mHa of the DMRG reference, and at 56-70 qubits the selected circuits use far fewer two-qubit gates than the transpiled LUCJ circuit.

entry.title: Real-time machine-learning decoders for fusion-based quantum computing
entry.summary: Machine-learning decoders for fusion-based quantum computing in real time arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper introduces PRISM, a transformer-based machine-learning decoder for fault-tolerant quantum protocols affected by both Pauli and erasure errors. It exploits the known locations of erasures and is benchmarked on surface, color, and quantum LDPC codes with distances up to 24. PRISM matches the logical error rates of integer-programming decoders while being significantly faster. An optimized FPGA implementation decodes distance-8 logical blocks with a 6.59 microsecond latency.

entry.title: Computing Power of Clifford and Ising Quantum Computers
entry.summary: Computational Power of Clifford and Ising Quantum Computers arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper extends efficient classical simulation of Ising quantum computers from braidings to measurements. It examines several definitions of efficient Clifford quantum computation that differ in how much of the input the circuit generator can access. If the generator sees the entire input, efficient classical simulation would imply that complexity classes P and PSPACE are separated. If it sees only the input length, Clifford quantum computers are shown to decide affine languages.

entry.title: Quantized memory of measurement records near the light cone of quantum circuits
entry.summary: Quantized memory of measurement records near the light cone of quantum circuits arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper studies the statistics of mid-circuit measurement outcomes in quantum circuits and shows they become exactly solvable near the light cone. In brickwork circuits, measurements along the light-cone edge form a two-state Markov chain, and the memory of the record is quantized to at most one bit per site of displacement. The authors also present a tomography-free witness of dual-unitarity and test the predictions on a 156-qubit superconducting processor. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show measurement-record memory near the light cone is exactly solvable and quantized, and report verification on a 156-qubit processor.

entry.title: Long-range correlated quantum errors from diffuson-correlated dephasing: how disorder-induced modes in conductors cause correlated qubit dephasing
entry.summary: Long-range correlated quantum errors from diffuson-correlated dephasing arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper shows that low-energy disorder-induced modes called diffusons in a diffusive conductor cause spatially correlated dephasing on qubits sharing that conductor. Using a Keldysh nonlinear sigma model, the authors derive the noise kernel in closed form, which decays as the inverse square of qubit separation and changes sign with pair orientation. In two dimensions, the worst-case correlated noise a qubit shares with an array grows logarithmically with array size, so standard fault-tolerance threshold conditions may no longer hold for large arrays. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose diffuson-correlated dephasing, derive a closed-form noise kernel, and argue it can violate fault-tolerance threshold conditions in large arrays.

entry.title: Rational quantum spectral filters via a repeat-until-success protocol
entry.summary: Rational quantum spectral filtering by repeat-until-success protocol arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper introduces a finite-memory repeat-until-success (RUS) framework for implementing rational spectral filters on a quantum computer, going beyond the polynomial transformations of QSP and QSVT. The protocol interleaves queries to a block encoding of a Hermitian operator with mid-circuit measurements. The authors exactly characterize which spectral filters can be realized upon acceptance and give a constructive compiler with memory and query-cost bounds. Applications to regularized resolvents and Lorentzian spectroscopy show query-cost advantages over a fixed-depth QSVT baseline. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use a finite-memory repeat-until-success protocol to realize rational spectral filters beyond QSP/QSVT polynomials, with an exact characterization, compiler, and reported query-cost compar

entry.title: FusionQ: A General Optimal Decoder for Ultra-Low-Latency Quantum Error Correction
entry.summary: FusionQ: A Generic and Optimal Decoding Framework for Ultra-Low-Latency Quantum Error Correction arXiv · Nov 10, 2026FusionQ is a decoding framework for quantum error correction that builds small local decoding problems around clusters of triggered detectors, rather than solving one large global problem. It expands a local problem only when its best solution uses virtual boundary errors, and then merges the local results into a single global correction. The authors prove that, with an exact minimum-weight local solver, the fused result equals the global most-likely error solution of the original model. Evaluations report that the exact-backend version matches the monolithic result on every shot and reduces decoding latency by overlapping local decoding with syndrome acquisition. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a fusion framework with a compositional optimality theorem matching global MLE, and report latency reductions across decoder backends.

entry.title: The wave equation and two-electron atomic wavefunctions
entry.summary: The wave equation and two-electron atomic wavefunctions arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies axisymmetric solutions of the classical wave equation in three spatial dimensions. It shows that these solutions correspond one-to-one with functions that annihilate the two-electron kinetic energy operator, written in coordinates relative to a fixed nucleus.

entry.title: Early state exclusion problem for 5×5 Jacobi matrices
entry.summary: Early State Exclusion for 5×5 Jacobi Matrices arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper examines a problem from quantum computing in which the quantum state to be transferred completely vanishes before perfect state transfer first occurs. The question was posed as open for one-dimensional quantum chains with an odd number n>4 of qubits. The authors present a solution for the case n=5. The proofs require only trigonometry, calculus, and eigentheory and inner products from linear algebra.

entry.title: A compiler for fault-tolerant quantum computing that keeps error-correction details inspectable
entry.summary: A Compiler for Fault Tolerant Quantum Computing arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper presents FTQC, an open-source MLIR dialect that represents logical qubits, syndromes, magic states, and Pauli frames as typed SSA values. It provides an error-correction-aware type system, a two-level lowering design, and resource analysis inside the IR, connecting to OpenQASM 3, QIR, Stim, and IQM hardware. Case studies across three code families show typed metadata makes code-specific decisions verifiable and retargetable, and decoding reduced logical readout error by 3.3 times on the 20-qubit Pathfinder at Oak Ridge National Laboratory.

entry.title: Neutron scattering study of how density affects one-dimensional quantum fluids
entry.summary: Neutron Scattering studies of the density dependence of One-dimensional Quantum Fluids arXiv · Nov 10, 2026Researchers confined helium-4 in a templated porous material pre-coated with a noble gas to achieve one-dimensional behavior, then studied it with neutron scattering. By varying the filling fraction of the one-dimensional core, they found the one-dimensional liquid always forms at a fixed density. The authors attribute the increase in filling to the liquid extending further along the one-dimensional direction.

entry.title: Exceptional points in non-Markovian quantum-state diffusion, from coefficient dynamics to state observables
entry.summary: Exceptional points in non-Markovian quantum-state diffusion: From coefficient dynamics to state signatures arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies how exceptional points of memory-coefficient equations in non-Markovian quantum-state diffusion (NMQSD) appear in different quantum-state observables. It uses a finite homogeneous lift to identify Jordan chains reached by causal initialization, and state reconstruction to determine which contributions survive in a given readout. Two models, common-bath qubits and a position-coupled oscillator, illustrate how the meaning of these exceptional points depends on the readout.

entry.title: Rényi Entanglement Entropy Dynamics and Eigenstate Thermalization: A theoretical study linking entanglement growth in quantum systems to the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis.
entry.summary: Dynamics of Rényi entanglement entropies and Eigenstate Thermalization arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies Rényi entropy dynamics in deterministic chaotic Floquet models, describing entanglement growth through eigenstates of the time-evolution operator. Inspired by the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, the authors combine random matrix theory, established ETH results and numerical tests in 1D to propose ETH-like ansätze for subsystem swap matrix elements. They show that in the thermodynamic limit, purity dynamics is governed by smooth, slowly varying functions, and discuss extensions to higher Rényi entropies.

entry.title: Finite measured entropy production need not imply finite microscopic irreversibility
entry.summary: Finite Measured Entropy Production Does Not Imply Finite Microscopic Irreversibility arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper constructs a driven quantum system in which a degenerate parametric oscillator below threshold repeatedly interacts with a thermal reservoir through bosonic ancillas, sustaining a positive heat current into the vacuum bath. A photon counter with finite efficiency, gated time bins and dark counts provides a common coarse-graining of forward and reverse trajectory laws. The authors prove that the observed relative entropy stays uniformly bounded as the bath temperature vanishes and is strictly positive at vacuum, while the hidden contribution scales as T times the vacuum heat current divided by k_B times the bath temperature. Measurable time asymmetry can therefore coexist with infinite microscopic irreversibility.

entry.title: Which data samples matter most when training quantum models?
entry.summary: Which data samples matter when training a quantum model? arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies quantum machine learning models from a data-centric perspective by establishing a quantum-compatible form of V-usable information. The metric measures how much information a model can extract from a dataset, allowing direct comparison of different models. The authors use it to identify which data points contribute most to learning and develop a preselection strategy for data subsets that improves training data efficiency.

entry.title: Measuring Quantum Chaos Using the Geometry of Hamiltonian Control
entry.summary: Quantum Control Geometry as a Metric of Chaos arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper introduces a quantum geometric framework that measures how sensitive many-body eigenstates are to allowed deformations of the Hamiltonian, constrained by spatial locality, symmetries, and conservation laws. The resulting geometric susceptibility serves as a quantitative metric of chaos, going beyond traditional binary diagnostics. For canonical models of quantum chaos, the authors find that minimal susceptibility, maximal eigenstate randomness, broad spectral response of local operators, and suppressed slow non-hydrodynamic structure all occur in the same region of Hamiltonian control space.

entry.title: Third-order quantum information from distributed randomized measurements
entry.summary: Third-Order Quantum Information from Distributed Randomized Measurements arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies quantum states shared among distant parties, using products of three outcome probabilities measured at the same local settings and averaged over independent local random unitaries to probe nonlinear properties without reconstructing the full density matrix. For any number of parties, the authors determine which third-order local-unitary invariant combinations these averages retain and which they cannot separate. By analysing the permutation symmetries of the distributed measurement protocol, the reconstruction reduces to symbolically inverting a 3 x 3 matrix, allowing nonlinear information to be extracted without inverting exponentially large matrices.

entry.title: Surface Codes Under Coherent Errors: Optimal Decoding and Finite-Size Effects
entry.summary: Surface codes with coherent errors: optimal decoding and finite-size crossovers arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies the surface code subjected to uniform coherent Z rotations followed by perfect syndrome measurements, a setting where finite-size effects make the asymptotic decoding threshold hard to extract. The authors identify two characteristic length scales governing finite-size behavior of Pauli decoding measures and coherent information, and show a broad intermediate regime as the rotation angle approaches π/4. For even code distances, they prove that maximum-likelihood Pauli decoding maximizes entanglement fidelity among all deterministic syndrome-conditioned recoveries, and that its threshold matches the one defined by coherent information.

entry.title: BPS Bootstrap: Constraining Simple Operator Expectation Values in Heavy BPS States
entry.summary: BPS Bootstrap arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper applies the large N matrix bootstrap to constrain expectation values of simple operators in heavy BPS states dual to classical geometries, working in N=4 SU(N) super Yang-Mills theory at large N and weak coupling. For the 1/2, 1/4, and 1/8-BPS sectors, the bootstrap yields large allowable regions consistent with an eigenvalue description at large charge. Preliminary results for a BMN truncation of the 1/16-BPS sector are also presented, but isolating black hole states within the bootstrap remains a challenge.

entry.title: Preparing quantum states by measurement and feedback: an exact first-passage theory
entry.summary: Frustration-free control for quantum-state preparation: an exact first-passage theory arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies how local measurements and feedback can autonomously prepare entangled many-body states, using Dicke states of N_q qubits as the example. Local singlet projectors define the constraints, and the dynamics closes exactly on the span of the N_q(N_q-1)/2 singlet-pair projectors, equivalent to a classical first-passage process. In one dimension the process is solved in closed form, with slowest rate 2[1-cos(π/N_q)] in units of the measurement rate.

entry.title: Kinematic Quantum Geometry: A Theory of Fast Degrees of Freedom Following Slow Coordinates and Velocities
entry.summary: Kinematic Quantum Geometry arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper presents kinematic quantum geometry, which describes fast degrees of freedom that adiabatically follow states parametrized by both the coordinates and velocities of slow degrees of freedom. It extends Born-Oppenheimer geometry, introduces mixed Berry curvatures, and modifies the effective theory for the slow degrees of freedom. The authors test the predictions for spinful particles in magnetic textures and for Dirac electrons in graphene coupled to an LC circuit. The framework is said to remain valid at large velocities beyond the perturbative regime if the kinematic states vary sufficiently slowly.

entry.title: Holographic drag force and entanglement membrane: geometry from information spreading
entry.summary: Holographic Drag Force and the Entanglement Membrane: Geometric Reconstruction and Information Spreading arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper establishes an exact geometric correspondence between the drag force on a moving heavy quark and the entanglement membrane that governs quantum information propagation. The leading nonlinear drag correction determines the butterfly velocity, and higher-order terms probe the membrane's geometry near the horizon. Combined with stochastic momentum broadening, these relations allow reconstruction of the bulk metric up to an overall scale.

entry.title: Time-direction entanglement entropy of free fermion ground states
entry.summary: Time Direction Entanglement Entropy of Free Fermion Ground States arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies the time direction entanglement entropy (TDEE) of free fermion quantum states over a time interval, computed from the reduced density matrix of the sub-Hilbert space that supports all time-evolved operators in that interval. Using the Fisher–Hartwig conjecture for Toeplitz matrices, the authors build an analytical framework for TDEE with discrete time steps. They report that for disorder-free one-dimensional systems TDEE can follow area, logarithmic or volume laws depending on gap, bandwidth and time step, while for 1D Anderson insulators it shows a Page-curve-like behavior. In the continuum time limit, the authors find logarithmic, area and sub-area laws for gapless fermions, band insulators and Anderson insulators, respectively.

entry.title: Field-induced phase matching for Josephson traveling-wave parametric amplifiers
entry.summary: Field-induced phase-matching in Josephson traveling wave parametric amplifiers arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper experimentally demonstrates a phase-matching method for Josephson traveling-wave parametric amplifiers (JTWPAs) that uses a homogeneous Josephson nonlinear medium. The approach exploits magnetic field inhomogeneity. The authors show that this inhomogeneity reverses the sign of the three-wave mixing nonlinearity and stabilizes parametric amplification. They propose the technique as a viable alternative to conventional phase-matching approaches.

entry.title: Quantum simulation of real-time bosonic dynamics using binary and unary position encodings on superconducting and trapped-ion hardware
entry.summary: Quantum simulation of real-time bosonic dynamics with binary and unary position encodings on superconducting and trapped-ion processors arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper compares two ways of encoding a bosonic position lattice in qubits, binary and unary, on IBM superconducting and IonQ trapped-ion processors. In a symmetric double-well test, unary circuits with about 200 two-qubit gates reproduce particle tunneling on both devices, while binary circuits with several thousand such gates do not. The authors report that the better encoding depends on grid size and evolution time.

entry.title: Measuring tripartite nonlocal magic via reflected and negativity spectra
entry.summary: Tripartite nonlocal magic from reflected and negativity spectra arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper studies when a tripartite pure state is local-unitary equivalent to a stabilizer state, namely when its marginal, reflected, and negativity spectra (up to signs) are flat. It quantifies this condition with anti-flatness, yielding a computable diagnostic of tripartite nonlocal magic that can be measured experimentally using randomized measurements. The authors also identify when this magic appears in non-abelian quantum doubles and in random tensor networks.

entry.title: Universal Fold Caustics in Anharmonic Matter-wave Lenses
entry.summary: Universal Fold Caustics in Anharmonic Matter-wave Lenses arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies how matter waves in a Bose-Einstein condensate focused by a short anharmonic lens form caustics, where classical ray focusing meets wave patterns. A semi-classical analysis shows that cubic aberration turns the harmonic focus into a fold caustic described by an Airy integral. Three-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii simulations show that mean-field interactions alter the near-focus density and momentum distribution, creating a secondary momentum-space feature. The authors estimate the effective interaction strength from 10^5 detected points, with a relative uncertainty of 2.7×10^-3.

entry.title: Termination at the second level of a PPT entanglement-cost hierarchy for two qutrits
entry.summary: Second-level termination of the PPT entanglement-cost hierarchy for two qutrits arXiv · Nov 8, 2026The paper proves that, for any two-qutrit quantum state, the semidefinite programming lower-bound hierarchy for PPT entanglement cost terminates at the second level. Under operations that preserve positive partial transpose, the zero-error asymptotic entanglement cost can therefore be computed by a semidefinite program with only three Hermitian matrix variables. The proof combines finite certificates checked in exact rational arithmetic with analytic estimates near the boundary of the parameter domain.

entry.title: Running time backwards in quantum systems and the limits set by environmental memory
entry.summary: Time Running Backwards, and Where It Stops: Superoscillations of Proper Time and the Memory of the Environment arXiv · Nov 8, 2026The paper studies a quantum system in a superposition of proper times, where post-selection produces a superoscillation of the time-dilation factor, so the system evolves for a proper time set by a weak value. The authors model a sealed cell of excited atoms, their radiation field and absorbing walls as one quantum object. They find that a decay younger than the environment's memory time can be witnessed as partly reversed, but beyond that time the effect fails because of the environment's spectral bandwidth rather than entropy.

entry.title: Parametric proof-carrying compilation for quantum error correction
entry.summary: Parametric Proof-Carrying Compilation for Quantum Error-Correction arXiv · Nov 8, 2026The paper presents PC-QEC, a proof-carrying compilation framework for quantum error correction parameterized by code distance and syndrome-extraction scheme, covering Standard, Flag, Shor and Knill schemes. For each family and scheme, code-algebra proofs and fault-aware Hoare proofs combine into a finite symbolic certificate whose size is independent of code distance. The authors demonstrate family-wide guarantees for five code families, and for the rotated Surface code one Standard Scheme certificate proves a distance lower bound d for every odd d≥3 in about 214 seconds on average. Lean 4 mechanizes the metatheory and exact circuit-level distances for canonical Surface, hypergraph-product and Toric code families.

entry.title: A paper on critical properties of EPR steering, a quantum entanglement effect
entry.summary: Critical properties of EPR steering arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies EPR steering, a phenomenon in quantum entanglement where one party's measurements can influence another party's conditional states. The authors prove that every PVM-critical entangled two-qubit state becomes steerable when two copies are available. They show that measurement entanglement, the number of measurements, and collective access each play different roles in revealing steering. The paper also constructs higher-dimensional states whose two-copy steering violation is unbounded, answering the amplification question posed by Hsieh, Liang, and Lee affirmatively. ★★★★ Notable: The authors claim every PVM-critical two-qubit entangled state becomes steerable with two copies, identifying a critical threshold where measurement entanglement vanishes, and report unbounded two-cop

entry.title: Dephasing-Induced Melting of Crystalline Spectral Form Factors: how energy dephasing in open quantum systems weakens long-range spectral order and how that order can be controlled
entry.summary: Dephasing-Induced Melting of Crystalline Spectral Form Factors arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper studies how energy dephasing in open quantum systems affects long-range spectral order. In spectral form factors, nearly crystalline spectra show sharp Bragg peaks at integer multiples of the Heisenberg time. The authors find that these peaks decay algebraically with revival order and dephasing strength over an extensive intermediate regime. Despite an extreme decoherence rate, the peaks persist up to the lifetime of nearest-neighbor coherences.

entry.title: A chiral waveguide model for error-correctable quantum computation
entry.summary: Chiral waveguide model for error-correctable quantum computation arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper builds a first-principles framework linking microscopic waveguide scattering to quantum error correction and algorithm performance. For polarization-encoded photons interacting with two-level atoms in a chiral waveguide, it derives an effective polarization quantum channel by tracing out frequency and uses it as the noise model for a rotated planar code, observing threshold behavior. The effective noise is strongly biased toward X errors, and incorporating the resulting logical errors into quantum phase estimation shows that a Hadamard-basis implementation improves algorithmic performance.

entry.title: Simulability frontiers of photonic quantum computing: the device size at which exact classical sampling becomes too slow
entry.summary: The simulability frontiers of photonic quantum computing arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper proposes the time a classical computer needs to draw one exact sample from a photonic device's output distribution as a common unit for comparing when such devices outgrow classical simulation. It defines the simulability frontier as the device size at which the fastest exact sampler yields one sample per second on a fixed machine. Using photonic-engines, an open-source GPU library, the authors measure frontiers on one NVIDIA H100 GPU: 38.3 single photons, 31.0 entangled photons from one emitter, and 41.5 squeezed photonic inputs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose exact per-sample sampling time as a common unit and report frontier values for several light sources.

entry.title: Closed-form hidden symmetry operators for the asymmetric quantum Rabi model and its two-photon and two-mode variants
entry.summary: The hidden symmetry operators of the asymmetric quantum Rabi model and its two-photon and two-mode variants in closed form arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper studies the asymmetric quantum Rabi model, a two-level system coupled to a boson mode, which shows level crossings when the bias is an integer multiple N of the mode frequency. These crossings are due to a hidden symmetry operator J, and the authors derive its closed form for every N. The operator is expressed as the parity of the symmetric model multiplied by a continuant built from N first-order operators. The same structure extends to the asymmetric two-photon and two-mode models, and the authors relate the formula to known recursion relations for J's coefficients.

entry.title: Boosting valley splitting in Si/SiGe Wiggle Well quantum dots with integrated stressor-gate designs
entry.summary: Enhancing valley splitting in Si/SiGe Wiggle Well quantum dots through integrated stressor-gate architectures arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper proposes patterned stressed thin films to generate shear strain in the quantum well of Si/SiGe quantum dot devices, aiming for controllable valley splitting. Finite-element simulations indicate that compressively stressed TiN films can produce shear strains above 0.1% at the quantum well, enough for valley splittings of hundreds of µeV in strain-assisted Wiggle Wells. The strain extends across multiple quantum dots and persists in realistic gate geometries, offering a fabrication-compatible route to scaling deterministic valley splitting to quantum dot arrays.

entry.title: GARI++: A General-Purpose Decoder for Quantum Error Correction
entry.summary: GARI++: A General-Purpose Decoder for Quantum Error Correction arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper presents GARI++, a two-stage decoding pipeline for quantum error correction. It reaches accuracy competitive with state-of-the-art methods on surface, bivariate bicycle and color codes without using ensembles. The second stage runs only when the first stage fails to converge, and it can be configured for the chosen code.

entry.title: Simulating quantum channels on digital quantum computers
entry.summary: Quantum Simulation of Quantum Channels and Applications arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper reviews the theory of quantum channels and proposes a method to simulate them on digital quantum computers, using the Choi-Kraus operator-sum representation and Stinespring dilation. It covers three applications: preparing mixed states, implementing POVM measurements, and simulating Markovian quantum dynamics. For the latter, the authors introduce a residual operator that builds a first-order quantum channel from the Liouvillian, allowing an Euler-like simulation without Trotterization. The simulations were run with IBM Qiskit's AerSimulator, and the code is available on GitHub.

entry.title: Universal semiclassical drift velocity of magnetic edge channels
entry.summary: Universal semiclassical drift velocity of magnetic edge channels arXiv · Nov 10, 2026Magnetic edge channels form at the edge of a two-dimensional electron gas in a magnetic field and travel unidirectionally along it, protected by topology. Using semiclassical quantization of electron skipping orbits, the paper shows that when many edge channels cross the Fermi level, their drift velocity equals half the electron Fermi velocity. This result holds for hard edges with isotropic dispersion and was checked numerically for massive electrons and massless electrons in graphene. Smooth electrostatically defined edges do not show this universality.

entry.title: Self-energy construction for chain representations of open quantum systems
entry.summary: Self-Energy Construction for Chain Representations of Open Quantum Systems arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper treats the self-energy as the environment's response to the system and examines how it transforms under shifts of the system–environment cut. For a semi-infinite chain with asymptotically uniform parameters, this transformation has a fixed point that defines the asymptotic boundary self-energy, whose spectral density is the Wigner semicircle. A pseudo-hyperbolic self-energy distance, invariant under cut shifts, is introduced and used to measure the error of finite damped-oscillator closures independently of the cut, offering a more accurate fitting scheme than time-domain correlation fitting.

entry.title: A unified neutral-atom architecture that can build any two-qubit gate
entry.summary: Unified architecture for arbitrary two-qubit gates with neutral atoms arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper proposes a unified architecture for two-qubit gates on neutral-atom quantum processors, covering the complete gate set. It relies on a single resource, an XXZ interaction with tunable anisotropy, combined only with single-qubit operations. The authors realize this tunable XXZ interaction using Rydberg atoms and pair it with optimally controlled global microwave pulses to implement the B, QFT, iSWAP, and √iSWAP gates, along with a continuous gate family interpolating from CZ to iSWAP via the B gate.

entry.title: An efficient classical algorithm for estimating OTOCs in chaotic quantum circuits
entry.summary: An efficient classical algorithm for OTOCs in chaotic quantum dynamics arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper presents a polynomial-time classical algorithm for estimating four-point and eight-point out-of-time-ordered correlators in typical one-dimensional random quantum circuits. It exploits dephasing caused by quantum chaos to suppress subleading terms in a rapidly converging series. At larger circuit depths, the authors report higher signal-to-noise ratio than recent 2D experiments by Google. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a polynomial-time classical algorithm for OTOCs in 1D random circuits, exploiting chaos-induced dephasing; numerical results are compared with Google's 2D experiments.

entry.title: Comparing Sequential and Parallel Ways to Share Quantum Advantage in Communication Tasks
entry.summary: Sequential vs parallel Strategies for Sharing Quantum Advantage in Communication Tasks arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies two experimentally feasible ways of sharing a quantum system among several observers, parallel and sequential sharing, to extract encoded information. With two observers, any statistics from parallel sharing can be reproduced sequentially, but with more observers some parallel statistics cannot be. The authors show that quantum advantage cannot be shared in parallel for a class of tasks with two decoding measurements, and discuss 3-bit random access codes, where parallel sharing becomes possible in the parity-oblivious variant. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show parallel and sequential sharing are equivalent for two observers but differ for more, with arbitrarily large gaps.

entry.title: Spin transport through chiral molecular bridges between quantum dots, with gate and holonomy analysis
entry.summary: Spin Shuttling Through Quantum-Dot Based Chiral Molecular Bridges: Gauge Constraints, Holonomy, and Quantum Gates arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper examines whether chiral molecular bridges between silicon quantum dots can serve as two-qubit entangling resources via the chirality-induced spin-selectivity effect. Using Makhlin invariants and a gauge argument, the authors show that a single chiral bond is locally equivalent to isotropic exchange and so is not a new entangling class. Breaking this gauge symmetry reveals chiral utility, including synthetic gradients and non-Abelian holonomy-based geometric gates.

entry.title: Single-particle resonances and eigenstate thermalization in periodic free-fermion lattices
entry.summary: One-Particle Resonances and Eigenstate Thermalization in Periodic Free-Fermion Lattices arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies particle-number fluctuations in energy eigenstates of the nearest-neighbour free-fermion model on a periodic cubic lattice. It proves that the particle-number variance is bounded by order NL^{d-1} for every eigenstate, and gives a corresponding eigenstate-thermalization estimate. At positive density the bound decays as the inverse linear size. The bounds are shown to be optimal in every dimension.

entry.title: Quantum-assisted selection of determinants for better ground-state energies
entry.summary: Quantum Residual Exploration for Selected Configuration Interaction arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper proposes a modular hybrid quantum-classical method that improves selected configuration interaction at a fixed final determinant budget. Quantum measurements supply complementary determinants, which are accepted only if they outrank classical candidates under a common energy criterion. The approach targets multistep excitations that perturbative methods may miss in strongly correlated systems. On the Quantinuum Reimei trapped-ion computer, measured proposals for H12 at a stretched geometry lowered the variational energy compared with classical-only selection.

entry.title: Higher tensor network states in 2D: a fundamental theorem for open boundaries
entry.summary: Higher tensor network states in two spatial dimensions: fundamental theorem for open boundary conditions arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper builds two-dimensional tensor network states by categorifying matrix product states, with bond spaces given by 2-vector spaces tied to the 2-cells of the lattice. Tensor network representations are defined as module categories over a free monoidal category encoding the lattice geometry. The authors prove that two representations generating the same states under suitable open boundary conditions are equivalent as module categories. They also introduce 2-injectivity, a categorified analogue of injectivity for matrix product states.

entry.title: Neutronic Field-Effect Transistor: a device controlling neutron-wave output via interference and spin
entry.summary: Neutronic Field-Effect Transistor arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper demonstrates a neutronic field-effect transistor (NFET), analogous to the Datta-Das electron spin transistor and atomtronic devices. The device is based on a perfect-crystal Mach-Zehnder neutron interferometer. Phase shifts are applied to both the spin and path degrees of freedom to control its operation.

entry.title: Apparent time advance of quantum clocks via postselection
entry.summary: Effective Time Advance of Quantum Clocks under Postselection arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper examines how quantum postselection can make a quantum clock appear to run ahead, reversing the usual relativistic time-dilation result. Using an analytically solvable quantum clock model, the authors postselect the center-of-mass motion and obtain an effective time advance through anomalous weak values. The analysis is extended to a weak gravitational field and illustrated with a hydrogen-like atom.

entry.title: Transferring usable energy over long distances using spin chains with weaker end couplings
entry.summary: Long-Range Ergotropy Transfer with Weakened Boundary-Coupling Spin Chains arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies how the extractable energy (ergotropy) of a quantum battery can be moved across a distance. The authors use spin chains whose couplings are weakened at the two boundaries, which create localized edge states that enable high-fidelity transfer within a given time. Both nearest-neighbor and long-range interaction models are examined, and weakening boundary couplings is reported to increase the maximum transferred ergotropy for long chains.

entry.title: All-to-all qubit coupling in a superconducting flux processor using adiabatic ZZ interactions
entry.summary: All-to-all connectivity via adiabatic ZZ interactions in a superconducting flux qubit processor arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper proposes a baseband-driven adiabatic ZZ gate that entangles any selected pair of flux qubits coupled through a common cavity, without requiring tunable couplers. The qubits stay biased at their flux sweet spot, while strong low-frequency drives applied through local flux lines tilt the quantization axes and generate a tunable longitudinal ZZ interaction. Numerical simulations report coherent gate errors below 10^-4 and robustness against frequency fluctuations.

entry.title: Finite projective classification of complex spinors using momentum maps
entry.summary: The finite projective classification of complex spinors via momentum maps arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper classifies projective orbits of complex spinors through the momentum map, covering irreducible spin modules in odd dimensions 1 to 11 and half-spin modules in even dimensions 2 to 14, the only cases with finitely many orbits. Representatives are built in the Clifford–Fock model as critical points of the squared momentum norm, and their momentum values distinguish the orbits. Completeness follows from Vinberg's theory of graded Lie algebras, yielding 1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5 orbits in odd cases and 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 4, 9 in even cases. In dimension fourteen, the closure order of the orbits is also determined.

entry.title: Topological states in fractals via a self-similar tensor network encoding
entry.summary: Topological states in fractals through a self-similar tensor network encoding arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper presents a tensor network method that exactly and compactly encodes Hamiltonians on self-similar fractal lattices, such as the Sierpiński gasket. The authors use this encoding to study a Chern insulator, the flux kagome model, confined to the fractal geometry and examine its topological states. The approach reaches much higher fractal generations than dense-matrix methods, resolving the density of states of a deep fractal with over 100 million sites.

entry.title: A paper on constructing quantum channels that preserve kappa-additivity and make outputs singular
entry.summary: Singularising quantum channels preserving kappa-additivity arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The authors build quantum channels by averaging unitary shift conjugations using kappa-additive probability measures on measurable abelian groups. The channels act on the duals of operator algebras generated by shifts and bounded measurable multiplication operators. They preserve kappa-additivity of quantum states and have a weak-* integral representation on this class. If the averaging measure vanishes on singletons, every output state is singular. An appendix proves the corresponding Fubini theorem for kappa-additive measures.

entry.title: Symanzik effective Hamiltonian for lattice quantum field theories
entry.summary: Symanzik Effective Hamiltonian for Lattice Quantum Field Theories arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper proposes a framework for constructing the Symanzik effective Hamiltonian of lattice quantum field theories directly from dimensional analysis and symmetries in the Hamiltonian formulation. It enables classification of all operators that can contribute at a given order in the spatial lattice spacing, and this list can be reduced using equations of motion and other identities. The framework is demonstrated for φ⁴ theory and pure gauge theory, with results consistent with earlier work for classical improvement. It is intended as a basis for a future non-perturbative improvement programme in the Hamiltonian formulation.

entry.title: Holonomy, spectral topology and detailed balance in classical and open quantum systems
entry.summary: Holonomy, Spectral Topology, and Detailed Balance in Classical and Open Quantum Systems arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This tutorial paper organizes band topology and non-Hermitian spectral theory around holonomy and applies them to mechanical metamaterials, chiral active fluids, stochastic networks and open quantum systems. Its central claim is that the spectrum of a linear generator can rule out detailed balance, forcing positive entropy production, but cannot determine how large dissipation is. The authors also propose benchtop tests for their statements.

entry.title: A proposed alternative framework to quantum theory
entry.summary: An Alternative to Quantum Theory arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper proposes an alternative framework that seeks to recover the empirical results of quantum theory from a holistic, scale-invariant ontology. It assumes only point particles in Euclidean space, described by ratios of masses, charges, and mutual separations, with shapes captured by a single scale-invariant function and no dynamical evolution. The author suggests the framework could in principle describe finite subsystems within an infinite configuration of particles.

entry.title: Universal two-qubit control across fridges over a 10 km optical link
entry.summary: Universal two-qubit control across dilution refrigerators via a 10-km coherent optical link arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper introduces a coherent optical link that transmits microwave control signals and phase references between two dilution refrigerators. Using a laser, a microwave-to-optical transducer, and an optical-to-microwave photodiode, the link carries control signals over 10 km of fiber. Through this link, the authors apply a universal gate set to a transmon qubit and a cavity qubit in another refrigerator and entangle them, reporting a Bell-state fidelity of 80.6%.

entry.title: Reachable and unreachable quantum precision limits in ultrastrong light-matter coupling
entry.summary: Attainable and unattainable quantum precision limits in ultrastrong light--matter coupling arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies how quantum precision depends on the gauge choice in ultrastrongly coupled light-matter systems. The transformation between gauges involves the coupling strength g, so each truncation gives a different family of results. The quantum Fisher information follows an exact parabola across gauges, and for harmonic matter it is minimized at a universal value set by the matter and cavity frequencies. Only the minimal-coupling bound can be reached, and the gauges differ by a factor of 9.6 with opposite trends.

entry.title: Discrete time crystals kept stable by limiting measurement noise
entry.summary: Discrete time crystals stabilized by bounded measurement noise arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper asks whether continuous weak measurement on a periodically driven, long-range interacting spin chain can sustain discrete time-crystalline period doubling. Typical quantum trajectories reach a state without subharmonic response, while the most-probable trajectory, with measurement fluctuations suppressed, shows robust period doubling. The authors introduce a bounded-noise protocol restricting measurement fluctuations to a finite window, finding that narrow windows preserve the order, intermediate windows give coexisting ordered and disordered trajectories, and wide windows destroy it.

entry.title: Calibration-free temperature sensing using strain-swept two-level defects in quantum devices
entry.summary: Calibration-free quantum thermometry with strain-swept two-level defects arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper examines whether intrinsic two-level defects in Josephson-junction barriers can serve as local thermometers by using the shape of their population response, without calibrating readout offset or contrast. It shows that for narrow sweeps the usable information scales with the fourth power of the sweep width. The approach is illustrated with a strain-swept defect in a Josephson junction.

entry.title: Deploying quantum key distribution on Sweden's national fiber network
entry.summary: Deploying QKD on the fiber links of the National Quantum Communication Infrastructure in Sweden arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper describes the deployment of quantum key distribution (QKD) on fiber links of Sweden's National Quantum Communication Infrastructure. The authors present procedures for characterizing fiber links and assessing their suitability for QKD. They relate measurable link properties to the factors that affect the secret key rate using a simplified model. They also report a successful one-month test on one of the links, confirming that QKD is feasible there.

entry.title: Commuting-check gauging for fault-tolerant logical measurements: adding completion qubits so local checks commute, enabling fault-tolerant logical measurement
entry.summary: Commuting-check gauging for fault-tolerant logical measurements arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper introduces completion qubits that make local checks commute for Clifford Z2 symmetries of qubit stabilizer codes, adding one per noncommuting pair while preserving the gauged code space, its distance, and the Clifford property of the checks. It extends the approach to qudits and shows that gauging and ungauging a distance-d code implements a logical measurement with circuit fault distance Ω(d) in O(d) rounds. The construction is demonstrated by gauging two toric codes into the D(D4) quantum double and back. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce completion qubits that make gauging checks commute, preserving distance and Clifford structure, with circuit fault distance Omega(d) for logical measurement.

entry.title: Testing whether gravity's phase dynamics are quantum under strong noise
entry.summary: Testing non-classical gravitational phase dynamics under strong dephasing arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper asks whether gravity must be quantum by examining its phase dynamics rather than entanglement, which noise often destroys. Within a dephased Bose–Marletto–Vedral setup, the authors prove an exact finite-time difference between gravitational conditional-phase evolution and any passive stochastic local-phase model driven by a classical mediator. The distinction persists, with modified sensitivity, when population-preserving classical measurement and feedback are included. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report an exact finite-time criterion separating gravitational conditional-phase dynamics from passive stochastic local-phase models under strong dephasing, extended to classical measureme

entry.title: High-rate quantum block turbo codes
entry.summary: High Rate Quantum Block Turbo Codes arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies new high-rate quantum block turbo codes. Quantum block turbo codes are an iterative decoding technique for concatenated quantum error-correcting codes in product form. The authors use different constituent codes and examine how changing code parameters and the order of constituent codes affects turbo decoding performance.

entry.title: A modular, loop-based photonic processor design for universal quantum computing.
entry.summary: Modular and Looping Quantum Photonic Processing Unit for Quantum Computing arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper proposes an architecture for a universal photonic quantum computer that is modular and built around a loop-based structure, which reduces the number of physical components needed. The authors show that the architecture is universal, deterministic, compatible with the quantum circuit model, reprogrammable, and capable of adaptive measurements. They demonstrate its operation through numerical simulations on specific examples, using machine learning to obtain some of its building blocks.

entry.title: A universal fault-tolerant quantum computing architecture using globally driven atom arrays
entry.summary: A Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing Architecture with Globally Driven Atom Arrays arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper proposes a universal fault-tolerant quantum computing architecture based on globally driven dual-species atom arrays. Qubits are selected through interspecies Rydberg interactions in a hybrid neutral-atom system, avoiding locally addressed quantum gates. The authors define a native instruction set, GRAIL, into which surface-code error correction and magic state cultivation are compiled, and report an error-correction threshold of 1.43% for the resulting quantum memory. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a globally driven dual-species atom architecture with a native instruction set, reporting a 1.43% threshold under a hardware-inferred noise model.

entry.title: Checking quantum circuit generators for equivalence across all parameters
entry.summary: Parameterized equivalence checking of quantum circuit generators via weighted automata arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper presents a method to check whether a quantum circuit generator matches a reference for all parameter values, under six equivalence relations. The generator builds circuits from a qubit count and a bit string. For ladder programs, the authors prove that above a computable threshold the circuit matrices form a uniform matrix product operator, a weighted automaton whose dimension does not depend on qubit count. Equivalence reduces to a zeroness check on a difference automaton, performed modulo primes. Experiments show the method finds errors missed by fixed-size checks and gave no incorrect verdicts.

entry.title: Fast, high-purity loading of barium ions using step-by-step isotope selection from natural sources
entry.summary: Rapid high-purity loading of barium ion via relayed selectivity from naturally abundant source arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This study presents a rapid method for selectively loading isotopes 137Ba+ or 135Ba+, which are promising ion qubits, from naturally abundant material. It uses a three-step, ultraviolet-free photoionization scheme: atoms are first selected on a narrow 791 nm transition, then resonantly excited at 554 nm, and finally ionized with an existing 532 nm Raman beam. No contaminant ions were detected during the experiment, and the resonant second step gave a high loading rate for the target ions.

entry.title: Semiclassical asymptotics of entanglement in torus-link quantum states
entry.summary: Semiclassical Asymptotics of Entanglement in Torus-Link States arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies the entanglement entropy of topological quantum states built from T_{d,dn} torus links in SU(2) Chern-Simons theory at level k. In the semiclassical limit k→∞, the authors derive the asymptotic behavior of moments of the reduced density matrix, finding that the limiting entropy is governed by the two edge regions while the bulk contribution is suppressed. The result is expressed using Hurwitz zeta functions and depends on k modulo n. For large d, the entropy reduces to a binary entropy set by left and right edge weights, and the two limits k→∞ and d→∞ are shown to commute.

entry.title: Proof of the QNEC without extra assumptions, using a weight
entry.summary: Proof of the QNEC, without assumptions and under a weight arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper completes a proof of the quantum null energy condition (QNEC) within the half-sided translations and modular inclusions framework, removing an assumption required by earlier proofs. It establishes that the relative entropy between the state of fields outside a stationary black hole and a Hartle-Hawking state is always a convex function of the horizon cut. The authors also present a generalization of the QNEC in which the Hartle-Hawking Hilbert space is replaced by one built on a weight. ★★★★ Notable: The authors remove an assumption from prior QNEC proofs and generalize the result to a weight-based Hilbert space.

entry.title: Encoding Optimization Objectives as Quantum Rotations
entry.summary: Rotational Encoding of Objective Functions for Quantum Optimization arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper introduces the Angular Rotational Counter (ARC), which encodes objective functions written as weighted sums of Boolean functions by accumulating quantum rotations on a single-qubit register. The authors apply this to build a quantum oracle for the state assignment problem of finite automata using a weighted Hamming distance cost. Across 26 benchmarks, compared with Boolean-based oracles, it reduces qubit count by a mean of 20.8%, gate count by 89.3%, circuit depth by 92.4%, and quantum cost by 90.6%.

entry.title: Long-distance secure direct communication using GKP qubits
entry.summary: Long-distance quantum secure direct communication with Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill qubits arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper proposes a quantum secure direct communication protocol that uses Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill encoding to transmit secret messages directly. It uses third-generation quantum repeaters to overcome the exponential photon loss. Numerical simulations indicate secure transmission beyond 1000 km at a 23 dB squeezing level. The authors also present a cost-based optimization framework balancing secure distance, secrecy capacity, and repeater resources.

entry.title: Super-resolution imaging via multiphoton correlation of thermal light
entry.summary: Super-resolution quantum imaging via multiphoton correlation arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper shows that classical thermal light can overcome the diffraction limit by correlating multiphoton subsystems detected in a Hanbury Brown-Twiss interferometer. The correlation function shows a narrowed peak or dip whose width can be tuned by the average photon number. Experiments achieved temporal and spatial super-resolution enhancements of up to 11.8-fold and 5.1-fold, respectively.

entry.title: Proof of the Rényi QNEC
entry.summary: Proof of the Rényi QNEC arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper proves the Rényi version of the quantum null energy condition (QNEC). The proof uses Araki-Masuda weighted L_p norms for all p > 2 and generalizes the algebraic proof for p=2. The authors also examine properties of the corresponding weighted conditional entropy. The p=2 limit corresponds to a conditional dynamical entropy originally defined in black hole dynamics. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend the algebraic QNEC proof to Rényi versions for all p>2 using weighted conditional Lp norms.

entry.title: An optimal quantum strategy for the 2-hat game
entry.summary: An optimal quantum strategy for the 2-hat game arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper studies the two-player hat game as a non-local game with two inputs and three outputs. The authors compute its quantum commuting value and show it equals the quantum value, which is (15+√33)/36, approximately 0.576238. The optimal quantum advantage is achieved using a shared non-maximally entangled qutrit state. The authors also determine the no-signalling value to be 2/3.

entry.title: Choosing model families and designing recovery gates in generator-based noise tomography
entry.summary: Model-family selection and recovery-gate design in generator-based noise tomography arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper treats selecting a noise model family in generator-based noise tomography as a hypothesis test whose minimum shot count has a closed form. It compares two platforms and sixty-four gate placements, finding that the required shots vary greatly with design and that placement mainly affects conditioning. The authors conclude that controlling systematic bias matters more than the raw shot count.

entry.title: Integer electron-count cuts for real-space pair-density representability: a convergent set of rigorous relaxations
entry.summary: Integer electron-count cuts in variational second-order reduced-density-matrix theory. II. A convergent hierarchy of rigorous relaxations for real-space pair-density representability arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper extends Part I by placing integer electron-count conditions in a convergent hierarchy of rigorous relaxations, defined by finite occupation linear programs on spatial partitions, for real-space pair densities at fixed one-particle density. Every level contains all representable pair densities and tightens under nested refinement, and their intersection characterizes pair densities admitting a symmetric N-particle probability-measure extension. In a fixed orbital basis, the levels give monotonically increasing lower bounds to the full configuration-interaction energy, which need not be reached.
